Asked whether alliance partner NCP's loss in the Thane Lok Sabha bypoll was a result of anti-incumbency against his Government, Deshmukh said "anti-incumbency cannot be judged on performance in a single constituency".

Heading: Battle of egos as Telangana votes - Indian Express
Content:
Southwest monsoon missed its date with the Kerala coast on Thursday but a top weather scientist sought to play the incident down saying it was not a "sign of worry."

"True, the onset over Kerala has not happened," Ajit Tyagi, Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said here.

The IMD had earlier forecast that the southwest monsoon will hit the Kerala coast on May 29, four days ahead of its normal June 1 onset.

Tyagi said Kerala had experienced a spell of rainfall but the IMD was waiting for the weather system to be more fully settled to declare the onset.

"The onset of monsoon is an activity which is important as it signals the arrival of rains over a major landmass. But it has nothing to do with the quantum of rainfall during the season," Tyagi said.

Heading: Speaks his mind, stands by it - Indian Express
Content:
Telangana voted in what is probably the largest ever byelection as 18 assembly seats and four Lok Sabha seats in the region went to the polls, recording a turnout of 52 per cent. There are 174 contenders for the assembly seats while 29 candidates are fighting for the Lok Sabha constituencies.

Though there is little in it for the Congress and the TDP—the K. Chandrasekhar Rao-led Telangana Rashtriya Samiti (TRS) is expected to walk away with the major chunk of seats—these two parties have little more than their egos at stake. The Congress has its back to the wall in the region' 10 districts because the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government is accused of reneging on its promise of initiating the process to carve out a separate state. The TDP is walking a tightrope on the T-sentiment. Chandrababu Naidu has not spelt his party's stance on the issue clearly, preferring to leave it for "consideration later as there are more important issue to dealt with first."

Bypolls had to be held for 16 assembly seats and four Lok Sabha seats after they fell vacant when TRS MLAs and MPs resigned in March.

On Thursday, Khanapur in Adilabad district recorded the highest voter turnout with 68 per cent followed by Jedcherla with 60 per cent turnout till 3 p.m. Urban constituencies reported a low voter turnout. Khairtabad in the heart of Hyderabad city recorded only 34 per cent while Secunderabad recorded 46 per cent.

Polling booths were empty till 11 a.m. in Khairtabad constituency, where P. Vishnuvardhan Reddy of the Congress is contesting. The bypoll had to be held after his father P. Janardhan Reddy's death.

In some booths, voters had to go back disappointed as their names were missing from the voters' list. Among those who returned without casting their votes were actor Murli Mohan and his family in Khairtabad constituency. Jedcharla in Medak district, from where YSR kicked off his campaign, recorded brisk polling throughout the day with a turnout of 60 per cent.

The four Lok Sabha constituencies too recorded good turnout with Hanamkonda in Warangal district recording 51 per cent, Karminagar, 40 per cent, Adilabad city 45 per cent and Warangal 50 per cent. TRS chief Chandrasekhar Rao is contesting from Karimnagar. The low turnout in here left the TRS chief a worried man.

The Election Commission ordered a case to be registered against the Chief Minister on charges of violating the code of conduct. The EC has also asked for details on TDP chief Chandrababu Naidu for holding a press conference after the end of campaigning.

Heading: UP’s merchant of votes - Indian Express
Content:
There are few politicians who speak their minds and fewer who stand by what they say. Madhya Pradesh's Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Gopal Bhargava is one politician who may not always say the right thing at the right time but is never shy of owning up.

A day after his sacrilegious comment that Brahmins don't need reservations and that they should leave quotas to beggars, he stood by his remarks saying he is free to express his opinion, especially when the platform is private (he said this at a function in the presence of the chief minister). The minister's bungalow in Bhopal was stoned, his nameplate gouged out and a police complaint was lodged against him for his "beggar" remark but the 56-year-old Brahmin MLA from Sagar is unfazed.

Never at a loss for words, Bhargava said all he meant was that Brahmins should not ask for reservation. He even dared Congress president Suresh Pachauri, a Brahmin, to contest against him from any seat. "The result will prove even backward castes are with me," he said in response to the Congress charge that the 'beggar' remark was an insult to those who are seeking reservation and those who had already got it.

A few months ago, he threatened to walk into the Pradesh Congress Committee office and beat Congressmen with 'chappals'. His outburst was in response to an agitation that the rival party launched against him for participating in a seemingly crude but traditional dance from Bundelkhand.

The BJP has done little about its outspoken minister, except cringe. His biggest folly on the floor of the Assembly was in the early 1990s when Sundarlal Patwa was the chief minister. When someone referred to a woman MLA from Jabalpur as 'kumari', he wanted to know if there was any proof. The controversy led to the disruption of the House and brought the chief minister to tears.

Govind Singh Rajput, a Congress MLA, said, "Though Bhargava projects himself as a messiah of Brahmins, he wants votes from all castes and pampers them all."

Heading: The Gurjjar face of Raje’s cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
As the Bahujan Samaj Party expands its base, reaching out to upper-castes and building what it calls a 'sarva samaj', Naresh Agarwal is poised to play an important role. The former Samajwadi Party MLA who was inducted into the BSP on Wednesday, has been made the party national general secretary and given additional charge of garnering support of the Vaishya (business) community to which he belongs.

In UP, the trading community that aligned with the Congress earlier, is firmly behind the BJP now. It is this vote bank that the BSP is trying to reach with the help of Agarwal and Akhilesh Das Gupta, another leader from the bania community.

Having the traders with them makes sound economic sense too. With traders now well organised under 'vyapar mandals' in every town of UP, they could contribute a lot to party coffers—a fact every party in the state recognises.

A seven-time MLA, Agarwal, who resigned from the Samajwadi Party last week, has also quit his Vidhan Sabha seat. His son Nitin, who too has joined the BSP, will contest the Hardoi Assembly seat vacated by him. Agarwal, meanwhile, will be contesting next year's Lok Sabha elections from Farrukhabad.

Agarwal's shift to the BSP is the latest in a series of political expediencies. Agarwal, first elected to the UP Assembly on a Congress ticket from Hardoi, floated the Loktantrik Congress Party (LCP) in 1997. The following year when a coup overthrew the Kalyan Singh government, the LCP's Jagdambika Pal was made chief minister and Agarwal deputy chief minister.

This new arrangement, however, lasted less than a week—the Kalyan Singh government was restored, Das removed and Agarwal continued to be a minister in the BJP government.

Agarwal then joined the Samajwadi Party, contesting the Assembly elections the following year from Hardoi.

Heading: A deadly infection under the microscope - Indian Express
Content:
Fifty-five-year old Kalulal Gurjjar, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Minister in the Vasundhara Raje-led government, is in a tough situation. While he is tied down by the BJP's stand on the Gurjjar issue, his son, Devalal Gurjjar, has openly come out in support of the Gurjjars.

On Wednesday, Devalal was put in preventive custody for "inciting violence among the Gurjjar community" in Bhilwara. Worse, he accused his father of being insensitive towards the Gurjjars. "He is under the influence of his second wife and is not paying any heed to the needs of the community," Devalal, the minister's son from his first marriage, said of his father. Ever since the Gurjjar agitation started last year, Devalal and his sarpanch wife have been critical of the BJP government. Devalal even courted arrest earlier this year in Bhilwara, the place that has the highest Gurjjar population in the state.

Area SP Mohan Singh says Devalal's active interest in Gurjjar politics is well-known in Bhilwara and on Wednesday, police found him "inciting the crowd for violence". But this is not a charge his father is free of either. The minister, who has been part of Rajasthan politics for at least four terms as MLA, was a much-favoured party loyalist until the Gurjjar agitations broke out last year. Then, the Chief Minister was reportedly upset with him for taking a stand against her. Gurjjar had criticised her government, of which he is a minister, for the police firing and had offered to resign.

This year, the minister treaded cautiously until Wednesday when his son made headlines much to the embarrassment of the Raje government. Party state secretary and woman Gurjjar leader Seel Dhabai, however, defended him, saying the minister and his son do not live together. "His estranged son is trying to create troubles for the father but the minister is with the party," Dhabai said.

But Kalu Lal, along with another minister in Vasundhara Raje's cabinet, Nathu Singh Gurjjar, has become the target of the community.

Heading: The other factor: Meenas - Indian Express
Content:
Peering into a 'phase contrast' microscope is Dr Reena Tilak, a scientist at the entomology division of the Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC). She is patiently picking on each hair of a mite that has been magnified to resemble a deadly insect. Deadly, yes, as this insect has had the armed forces worried about the emergence of 'scrub typhus', a disease that is known to have changed the course of a World War.

To be designated by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) as the nodal 'rickettsial disease centre for the country', Tilak and her team at the AFMC have been painstakingly poring over thousands of specimens that are being collected from Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, parts of Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand for evidence of 'scrub typhus'.

Rickettsial infections are caused by an unusual type of parasitical bacteria. Most of these infections are spread through ticks, mites, fleas or lice and the symptoms are fever, severe headache and rashes develop after being bitten by the mite. But since the symptoms are very common to diseases like malaria, scrub typhus has not been diagnosed, says Col R Bhalwar, Head of the Department of Community Medicine, AFMC. He explains that antibiotics are given as soon as the doctors suspect an infection and the patient recovers. Scrub typhus is prevalent in the north and north western parts of the country and is transmitted by the bite of the larval trombiculid mite.

Scrub typhus fever was first documented by an Indian army survey and in 1945, a field typhus team was raised under the South East Asia Command. According to Tilak, troops were known to retreat as the infection was usually fatal. Records point out there was a high mortality rate due to scrub typhus in WWII in the China-Burma-India theatre of operations.

While no there are typhus cases at present, the Armed Forces Medical Services has raised concern over its re-emergence, especially as troops move around in areas of heavy and low lying scrub vegetation. Contact with this mite can cause immense irritation.

The symptoms are either overlooked or misdiagnosed, says Tilak, who, for the past year, has been mapping mites across north India.

"If this disease is not detected early, it can lead to multi organ failure," says Tilak, who has trained public health doctors posted at the Station Health Organisations in the North.

Col Bhalwar has even urged the doctors to send them the patient's blood samples for investigation apart from the thousands of infected mites that are under microscopic examination at AFMC.

Heading: Lt Gen Lamba takes charge of 21 Corps - Indian Express
Content:
In the ongoing Gurjjar protests in Rajasthan-surfacing a year after a similar agitation for Scheduled Tribe status-there seems to be a distinct refrain: don't mention the rival Meena community.

"We are not competing with anyone. Our agitation has nothing to do with anyone, not even the Meenas. We are fighting our battle with the state government," insists Gurjjar leader Kirori Singh Bainsala, who is spearheading the agitation in Bayana.

After last year's bitter experience when the Meenas—a community that enjoys ST status but does not want Gurjjars to get it—clashed with the Gurjjars, Bainsala and his men seem to be treading cautiously. While Sikandara and Bayana reel under heavy protests that spread to other parts of the state by Tuesday, the protests began, in a strange coincidence, in places where there aren't too many Meena-dominated villages. Across Bayana, where thousands of Gurjjars continue to block trains, Meena villages are few and far between. Sikandara, where the police firing claimed more than a dozen lives and where Gurjjars are still sitting on the national highway with six corpses, is at least 35 kilometres away from the Meena-dominated belt of Mahwa.

Interestingly, Badabujurg village, on the Khedla road in Mahwa, is home to BJP leader K.L. Meena. Here, the Meena community is fuming. "If you think Meenas will stand and watch Gurjjars being given sops by the government, you are mistaken. There is no denying the fact that once they try encroaching our ST category space, we'll open a war," said Prabal Meena, a Badabujurg resident.

The community doesn't mind Vasundhara Raje's recommendation of 4-6 per cent quota for Gurjjars. "We are not opposed to Gurjjars getting reservation benefits. But we won't tolerate their inclusion in the ST category. As long as the state government is doing our job, we will watch. The day it stops, we'll start," Kamal Prasad Meena, another Badabujurg resident states with a grin.

It all began in 1999 when then prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee announced OBC status for Jats. The Jats are now backing the Gurjjars' demand for ST status, which leaders from both the Congress and the BJP say is not a good sign. "Once one community's demand is met, other communities will stand up and start agitating. It's like opening a Pandora's box," says a state BJP leader. The fears are not unfounded. After the Gurjjar agitation last year, Chief Minister Raje's office was flooded with demands for reservations from communities like Nayaks, Nais, Malis, Raibaris and Rawats—several of whom share OBC status with the Gurjjars.

Moreover, Gurjjar youths openly talk about how the Meenas have reaped the benefits of ST status over the years while they have stayed backward. "Meenas have IAS and IPS officers. Many doctors in state PHCs are Meenas. But look at us. We don't even have enough to eat," says 17-year-old Yogendra Singh Gurjjar, who has bunked school in neighbouring Boondi to take part in the Gurjjar agitation.

Heading: High-security number plates for new vehicles from November - Indian Express
Content: Lieutenant General Arvinder Singh Lamba has taken over command of the Bhopal-based 21 Corps. The officer is an alumnus of Defence Services Staff College and has undergone a course at the Royal College of Defence Studies in the United Kingdom. He commanded a Mountain Brigade in Nagaland, Manipur and an Infantry Division on the western border during Operation Parakram.

Heading: 14 more village tourism sites soon - Indian Express
Content:
Almost six years after the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways notified the introduction of High Security Registration Number Plates (HSRNP)—touted as one of the best anti-theft systems for vehicles—the ambitious plan will finally set take off in six months.

Starting this November, all new vehicles in the country will have to come equipped with these sophisticated number plates, while in-use vehicles will have to replace their current plates with HSRNPs within two years, said a senior official from the Ministry. It is believed that the measure will help keep a check on vehicle thefts and will allow authorities to track stolen vehicles.

The HSRNP scheme had been on hold with the tender process in several states drawn into litigation over the selection of vendors. All these cases were finally referred to the apex court, which recently directed the Centre to take a decision on implementing the scheme within six months. "We will be writing to all states very shortly to implement the HSRNP scheme," said a Ministry official.

The tamper-proof number plates are estimated to cost about Rs 2,500 per vehicle and cannot be easily removed and replaced.

The HSRNP concept dates back to 1997 when the Standing Technical Committee of Central Motor Vehicles Rules recommended that they be instated by 1999. Before doing so, the Committee studied the prevalent security features on number plates in different countries. The Ministry also engaged several agencies to shortlist vendors to manufacture these number plates and notified the scheme in 2001.

Not easy to tamper with

•Unique laser numbering containing the alphanumeric identification of testing agencies and manufacturers.

•Embossed registration numbers as well as chromium hologram on the aluminium plates.

•Rear registration plates fitted with non-reusable snap locks to make them tamper-proof.

•A third chromium-based registration plate in the form of sticker to be attached to the windshield. It will contain the number of the engine and chassis, along with the name of the registering authority. If tampered with, it self-destructs.

•In front and rear registration plates, the letters 'IND' in blue hot-stamped to the plates.

•A retro-reflective film, bearing a verification inscription 'India' at an inclination of 45 degrees.

Heading: Nicotine monitors released - Indian Express
Content:
Encouraged by the response to its rural tourism project, the Government has identified 14 more village sites which would be opened for foreign tourists in the near future. Spread over six states, these new sites would add to the 15 model villages that already exist and are attracting an impressive number of tourists.

The Tourism Ministry had launched its ambitious rural tourism project last year in a bid to bring the benefits of a tourist destination to far-flung and under developed areas of the country. The idea was to showcase India's arts and crafts in its natural setting and promote sustainable tourism. Traditional accommodation and food were to be the major attractions while ensuring clean sanitation facilities and convenient communication linkages with urban centres.

Accordingly, the ministry had spent Rs 50 lakh in each site for setting up the necessary physical infrastructure while another Rs 20 lakh was used for training and sensitisation of local population. Employment generation and infrastructure development were necessary byproducts of this project.

Heading: Centre to set up panel to help Bhopal gas leak victims - Indian Express
Content:
After several hurdles, a consignment of air-monitoring devices that calculate nicotine levels in buildings has finally reached the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (IUATLD), which is coordinating with the Health Ministry in its fight against tobacco.

With the aim of making Delhi, Chennai, Chandigarh and Ahmedabad smoke-free, Johns Hopkins University sent 160 air-nicotine monitors—free of cost—for each of the four cities about two weeks ago, but the cargo got stuck with the customs department in India.

"It was not a dutiable thing and hence we pleaded for it to be released," said a senior official in the Health Ministry. On Monday, however, the IULTD received the devices. "The equipments have been received and will be sent to the cities soon," said Dr P P Mandal, regional programme coordinator of the organisation.

Heading: HC nod to Kamal Haasan’s magnum opus - Indian Express
Content:
The Government has agreed to set up a panel to help victims of the 1984 Bhopal gas leak, which has till now killed more than 15,000 people.

On Thursday morning, Minister of State in the PMO Prithviraj Chavan visited Jantar Mantar where the Bhopal survivors have been protesting for the last two months and read out a two-page statement authorised by the Prime Minister. The statement said India would press the US company which now owns Union Carbide to clean up the site.

Though their top demand of setting up a commission to carry out medical, economic, social and environmental rehabilitation of the Bhopal gas victims was addressed in the statement, the group of activists camping in the Capital were not completely satisfied. While the Central Government will work on setting up the commission, "the Government of Madhya Pradesh is also being asked to prepare a detailed action plan pertaining to the rehabilitation schemes of Bhopal gas victims".

The group will send a letter to the Prime Minister with the final draft of the Commission on Bhopal Bill, to be passed in Parliament. The proposed Commission will have survivors' representatives and will function for the next 30 years at least. The protestors said they would discuss the PM's response and decide whether they will continue their dharna here.

The PMO statement added that on the demand of provision of clean drinking water in 14 localities near the former Union Carbide plant, a project under the Jawaharlal Nehru Urban Renewal Mission has been sanctioned at an estimated cost of Rs.141.8 million.

But Satinath Sarangi, an activist, complained: "Legal action against Union Carbide and Dow Chemical, the main culprits of the gas tragedy, has not yet been decided." The PMO's statement only said the matter of legal action against Dow Chemical on environment and health of the surviving victims is still pending before the Madhya Pradesh High Court.

Union Carbide and its former chairperson Warren Anderson, both of whom face charges of culpable homicide and grievous assault, are absconding from Indian courts since 1992. No fresh attempts have been made by the Government to enforce their appearance in court.

The PMO statement said the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals has already filed an application requesting the court to direct Dow Chemical and associated companies to deposit Rs 100 crore as an advance for environmental remediation. It said the Union Ministry of Family and Health Welfare will be asked to continue research work on the adverse effects of the gas leakage on the health of the surviving victims through the Indian Council of Medical Research.

Heading: Bhatia wants Parsvnath to bail out Nanocity - Indian Express
Content:
Dasavatharam, actor Kamal Haasan's so-called magnum opus, is all set to hit the screens after it cleared the legal hurdle on Thursday.

A High Court Bench here dismissed a petition filed by the International Sri Vaishnava Dharma Samrakshanna Society (SVDSS), represented by president Swamy Govinda Ramanuja Dasan, demanding change of movie title and deletion of certain scenes from the movie. Justices K Venkataraman and M Satyanarayana ruled that Dasavatharam was an ancient name without any intellectual property rights attached, and as such, nobody could object to it as the title of a movie. The court also refused to direct the Censor Board to delete certain portions, as the petitioners themselves have not watched the movie.

Based on the clippings shown in a private channel, the petitioner had contended that the movie, with its portrayal of clashes between Vaishnavites and Saivites, may lead to tensions between the believers of the two schools of thought.

However, the Bench refused to entertain the contention, stating, "The petitioner cannot demand deletion of scenes since they have not watched the film." Some of the objections raised by the petitioner was an "imaginary assumption" observed the Bench, adding that some of the scenes were merely fiction stemming out of imagination.

Denying the allegation that the movie offended religious sentiments, the defence counsel appearing for producer 'Oscar' K Ravichandran and director K S Ravikumar maintained that the movie glorified the existence of God as the supreme power.

Heading: Modi asks PM to pick a leaf out of Shastri’s fasting notes - Indian Express
Content:
Failing to kick-start its ambitious Rs 1,850 crore Nanocity project -building a sustainable city with world-class infrastructure - in Haryana's Panchkula district, Hotmail founder Sabeer Bhatia's company Nanocity Developers Pvt Ltd has initiated talks with private property developers to bail out the project.

Confirming the company has finalised Parsvnath Developers for the venture, Naval Bhatia, director of Nanocity Developers, said that no decision has been taken on Parsvnath's equity stake in the project, but that the details should be worked out next month when Sabeer Bhatia will visit India to help push along the negotiations.

However, Parsvnath seems to be treading with caution, as any such development has to be listed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Though it confirmed a tie-up with Nanocity, its officials refused to divulge any details.

Surprisingly, Parsvnath claimed to be unaware about whether any land out of the 11,000 acres proposed to be part of Nanocity have been acquired by Bhatia's company. Nonetheless, Naval Bhatia said that they are verifying sales deeds for about 500 acres of land bought by them in Panchkula for the project.

Besides the issue of land, Bhatia's strategy of trying to hype his ongoing negotiations with builders to get the best deal may spell trouble for the talks, reveal sources in Parsvnath. Nanocity Developers holds 90 per cent equity in the project while the remaining 10 per cent is held by the Haryana State Industrial Development Corporation (HSIIDC).

Heading: Yeddyurappa to take oath today, will induct Muslim into Cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi has done it again: this time he's done a Lal Bahadur Shastri on Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. Targeting the PM for his lack of direction, Modi urged him to request the nation to observe a weekly fast in order to tide over the prevailing price rise and food shortage.

Speaking at a public function in Bilimora town of south Gujarat, Modi sought the PM's social leadership in urging the nation to observe a one-meal day at least once a week, Modi demanded Singh's resolve and inspiration to fight against the national issue.

"It is our biggest misfortune that there is no political will at the central level to give us any leadership and direction. In a similar situation years ago when the nation had passed through a food scarcity, the then Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri had appealed for a weekly fast and got people's support. Can't the PM make a similar appeal now?" he said while unveiling a statue of the Maratha chieftain Shivaji at the city centre.

Heading: In wake of quake and Finger Point, Pranab to visit China - Indian Express
Content:
B S Yeddyurappa will create history when he takes oath as chief minister of a full-fledged BJP Government in a southern state on Friday. The BJP leader, who campaigned on a non-Hindutva platform on one hand and also made Gujarat CM Narendra Modi to tour the state extensively, will induct a Muslim minister into the Cabinet.

"The Muslims supported us in the elections. One Muslim minister is a certainty when I take oath as CM," Yeddyurappa told The Indian Express. Dr Mumtaz Ali Khan, who heads the state BJP minority wing, is likely to be sworn in along with the CM, say sources.

Karnataka will become the second BJP-ruled state after Rajasthan to have a Muslim minister. Five states ruled by the party — Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Chhattisgarh — don't have any representation from the Muslim community.

BJP vice-president Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi called this a "positive beginning". "At times we are not able to get winnable candidates, but this definitely is a positive beginning," he told this newspaper.

The BJP had not fielded any Muslim candidate in Karnataka, though. "But I made a promise to this effect during the elections," said the CM-designate. Asked if his Government would reach out to the Muslims on contentious issues like the Bababudangiri hills, dubbed as the Ayodhya of the South by the VHP, he said, "Of course, I would hold talks. Let this Government settle down first."

While the party often cites Bharatiya Jan Sangh founder Deen Dayal Upadhyay's "Muslims-are-the-flesh-of-our-flesh-and-blood-of-our-blood" statement to cite its intent, it has done precious little to integrate the largest minority community into the party. Former party president Bangaru Laxman had set out on an ambitious "Integrate Muslims" experiment that fizzled out after he figured on the Tehelka tapes. In the present BJP set-up, while Naqvi is known as an excellent organiser, the party has Shanawaz Hussein and Najma Heptullah as two other prominent Muslim leaders.

Meanwhile, thousands of BJP activists are expected to throng Yeddyurappa's swearing-in ceremony. A galaxy of front-ranking BJP leaders, including L K Advani, Rajnath Singh, Venkaiah Naidu, Arun Jaitley and Sushma Swaraj, are expected to be present during the ceremony.

The party won 110 seats out of 224 in the state Assembly, falling short by three numbers for simple majority. The party will also reward independents with ministerial berths. Governor Rameshwar Thakur will administer oath of office and secrecy to the new ministers.

Heading: Badal ‘waits’ inside as cops arrest Cong leaders - Indian Express
Content:
In the complex backdrop of India's flourishing trade relations with China and its significant contributions to earthquake aid for the country—while also contending the Chinese government's fresh claims on the Sikkim border— External Affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee will embark on a four-day official visit to China on June 4. It is his first visit during the UPA's tenure.

In Beijing, he will meet the Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs Yang Jiechi to discuss bilateral relations and regional and international issues of mutual interest, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Thursday. Mukherjee will also meet Chinese premier, Wen Jiabao. Both sides are likely to sign a couple of agreements, including the renewal of an agreement on the Brahmaputra river.

Significantly, Mukherjee will visit the city of Guangzhou, the capital of Guang Dong province and a commercial hub, to inaugurate a second Indian consulate (the first is in Shanghai). This signals the increased trade relationship between India and China and is the outcome of a reciprocal arrangement between the two countries.

China is also opening a second consulate in Kolkata, after Mumbai. The Indo-China bilateral trade has already surpassed the previously set target of $ 40 billion by 2010, and is now aiming at $ 60 billion.

The visit comes just after China suffered a major earthquake in the Sichuan province on May 12, as a response to which India reached out to the country with $ 5 million as aid and dispatched two aircrafts carrying tents, blankets and other relief materials.

Yet, despite relatively friendly relations between the two countries, tensions regarding China's claims over Sikkim's northernmost tip—the Finger Point area—have arisen recently.

This development has come when the already unresolved border dispute is being talked over by the two countries through their Special Representatives.

Heading: 2 killed as violence mars Gurjjar stir - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's plans to roll out the proverbial red carpet for Congress leaders, scheduled to protest outside his official residence on Thursday, came to a naught thanks to the overcautious Chandigarh Police.

As soon as the Congress leaders ventured out of the party office, with Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee chief Rajinder Kaur Bhattal in the lead, and tried to walk towards Badal's residence, the UT police arrested them on the apprehension that they would breach peace. The Congress leaders, including two sitting MPs, 40 MLAs and heads of frontal organisations, were let off after about two hours.

Meanwhile, Badal, who claimed to have cancelled "important engagements to personally welcome the opposition leaders", kept waiting for the protestors. The Chief Minister claimed he had made "adequate arrangements" for the Congress leaders. The Government had set up a "pandal" at the vacant space opposite the Chief Minister's residence, with two specially-marked chairs being kept for Bhattal and former Chief Minister Capt Amarinder Singh.

Capt Amarinder's supporters, incidentally, had already indicated his unwillingness to participate in the protest in view of his ongoing rift with Bhattal.

The Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee had called for the dharna to protest against the "unprecedented violence and murder of democracy" by the SAD-BJP Government in the recently-held panchayat and Amritsar Assembly bypoll. On May 24, the party had staged a similar dharna outside Badal's residence.

Heading: Rahul assured nothing: Gurjjar delegation - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Gurjjar leader Kirori Singh Bainsla on Thursday said he could consider talking to the Rajasthan Government provided it made a "proper proposal", at least two persons were killed, one of them in police firing, and 14 policemen injured as sporadic violence marred Gurjjars' agitation in Delhi and Haryana. In both the states normal life was disrupted by a rail and road blockade enforced by the community members.

Rajasthan, the epicentre of the movement which claimed 39 lives in the past one week, was, however, comparatively peaceful barring a bandh in Jaipur that evoked partial response and stray incidents of road blockade in five districts.

With no signs of an early end to the week-long Gurjjar agitation demanding ST status, BJP general secretary in charge of the state Gopinath Munde told reporters in Jaipur that the Rajasthan Government was ready for fresh talks with Bainsla. Munde's statement came after his day-long talks with ruling BJP and state Government functionaries, including Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje.

An invitation for talks would be extended to the protestors led by Bainsla in Pilupura, Munde said.

One person was killed when the police opened fire on agitators who blocked traffic on national highway at Patti Kalyana in Panipat district of Haryana for hours while an elderly man died in the stampede triggered by the police action.

Haryana's Additional Director General of Police (law and order) V B Singh, who visited the spot, said some agitators were carrying arms and they too opened fire. He said 14 policemen were injured, three of them seriously, in the skirmishes with the agitators.

Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the circumstances leading to the death of the two persons.

Appealing to the Gurjjar community to conduct their agitation in a peaceful manner, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati asked the Centre and Rajasthan Government to work on a "middle path" to find a solution to their problems.

"The Central and state governments should discuss the matter and adopt a middle path to find a solution to the demands of the Gurjjars," she told reporters in Lucknow.

LJP chief Ram Vilas Paswan also assured support to the Gurjjars' demand and said he would take up the issue with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and UPA Chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

Meanwhile, talking to reporters in Karwadi in Rajasthan, Bainsla suggested it was time to exclude some castes which had already benefited from quota and include new ones that "deserve and require" it.

Heading: Stir cloud over BJP national meet, Karnataka show - Indian Express
Content:
While the Congress and BJP are engaged in a verbal duel over Rajasthan Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje's letter to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh regarding Gurjjar community's demand, Gujjar Arakshan Sangharsh Samiti (GASS), which had sent a delegation to meet AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday, has said they received no assurance from the Congress leadership about their demand for ST status.

The Amethi MP referred the delegation to AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh who also failed to give any clear commitment, according to GASS spokesperson Roop Singh.

"While Rahul Gandhi referred the delegation to Digvijay Singh, the latter only criticised the state Government and offered sympathy for us. We wanted the Congress' intervention to ensure a proper answer to the state Government's letter to the Prime Minister. If the letter is incomplete, the Centre can ask the state Government for a new letter. But there was no concrete assurance," Roop Singh told The Indian Express.

On Thursday, he led another delegation to BJP leader Vijay Goel who assured them that the party would try to solve their problem after the party's central leaders return from Karnataka on Saturday.

Meanwhile, as the BJP sought to put the onus for solving the current crisis on the Centre saying giving ST reservation was the prerogative of the Union Government, the Congress shot back saying Raje had not made any clear recommendation. "The Chief Minister should have written to the SC/ST Commission, which would have forwarded it to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs before the Cabinet could consider the recommendation," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari told reporters.

Heading: Bihar rebels flex muscle - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP will use its national executive, beginning here on Sunday, to pitch itself as the frontrunner for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections. While the Karnataka win is expected to keep the mood upbeat, the party is at the same time worried over the Gurjjar agitation that showed no signs of abating on Thursday.

The BJP, meanwhile, said the Centre had "rejected" Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje's letter recommending reservation for Gurjjars. "The Centre has rejected Rajasthan Chief Minister's letter recommending reservation for Gurjjars even without discussing or studying it," party leader Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi said.

"The Congress-led Government is more interested in reaping political gains out of the agitation rather than carrying out its constitutional responsibilities. It is trying to add fuel to the fire," he added.

Three resolutions are likely to figure in the executive. While the political resolution will focus on the "highway to victory", suggesting that the party was well ahead of others for the parliamentary polls, two others on inflation and foreign policy will come down heavily on the Centre.

All seven BJP chief ministers will attend the meet which is also likely to discuss the ongoing process of identifying candidates for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections. The meet will discuss the Centre's "discrimination" against the BJP-ruled states. The party will also formalise its strategy for the forthcoming polls in Delhi and BJP-ruled states of Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.

Heading: Hand over bodies of dead: Pilot to Raje - Indian Express
Content: The Bihar BJP rebels, who have been asked to lie low till the party national executive gets over on June 2, continued their muscle flexing on Thursday. A leading member of the group, camping in Delhi, claimed the anti-Sushil Kumar Modi MLAs would quit the party en masse if their demand is not met. The rebels claim support of around 35 of total 55 party MLAs in the state. The central leadership, while conceding that Modi has allowed the JD(U) to grow at the BJP's expense, is ready to accommodate the rebels' demands, except his removal. The rebels, however, contend that anything less than Modi's head is not acceptable to them.

Heading: Trinamool’s TN unit wants to have truck with Jaya - Indian Express
Content:
Dausa MP and prominent Gurjjar leader Sachin Pilot on Thursday demanded that the Vasundhara Raje Government hand over bodies of those killed in the police firing last week to their relatives so that they could be "honourably cremated".

Pilot said there were five bodies with the police in Bharatpur and 14 in the mortuary of the SMS Hospital in Jaipur. "The state Government has not given permission for their postmortem for the last seven days. Bereaved family members are helpless and inconsolable. The state must hand over the bodies to the family members so that they can be honourably cremated," said Pilot. "While living persons are being prosecuted, even the dead are being punished by the Government. Even if you kill a soldier from the enemy side, you hand over the body with respect. It is not about caste or community; it is about humanity. How long can this state-sponsored terrorism go on?" he asked. The Dausa MP's attempt to reach the grieving families has so far been thwarted by the state Government, which has reportedly not allowed him to go to affected areas.

Meanwhile, senior BJP leader Gopinath Munde said the state Government has asked the Medical and Health Department to conduct postmortem on 14 bodies lying at the SMS Hospital. They will be delivered to their relatives for last rites, Munde said.

Heading: VIPs called cops, tried to help Susairaj - Indian Express
Content:
As her NDA partner, the BJP, has made its foray into the southern state of Karnataka, Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress too has struck its roots down south, with its Tamil Nadu unit coming into existence. A delegation from Tamil Nadu who have styled themselves as All India Thirunamool Congress met Mamata Banerjee at her south Kolkata residence on Wednesday night.

The delegation, which is said to be keen on entering into an alliance with AIDMK for the Lok Sabha polls in 2009, requested Mamata to talk to AIDMK chief Jayalalithaa.

"We set up the party three years ago. Recently, Mamataji's agitation at Singur and Nandigram — her 26-day fast on the issue — has enhanced her image tremendously. In just one year, the number of our members has doubled up — from 12,000 last year to 25,000 now. We are engaged in various agitations on issues like price hike and corruption. We have told Mamatadidi if she comes and addresses rallies, it will boost the workers' morale. And it's she who will have to take up the issue of alliance with Jayalalitha," said C K Soman, state secretary of TMC (TN), adding they congratulated her on her spectacular success in the recent panchayat elections.

Mamata is sending former MP Dinesh Trivedi to Chennai on June 26 to see how her party unit is faring. "I have made Dinesh Trivedi in-charge of our Tamil Nadu unit. Let him go, assess the political situation there and give me his report and then I will decide."

Mamata's simplicity and honesty have impressed many. "In our state most leaders are corrupt. But look at her. I am astonished to see her residence. I could not believe that this dilapidated house belongs to a national leader like Mamata," said Jaya Kumar, a small businessman from Kancheepuram, who was part of the delegation.

R Muthammal, state secretary of Tamil Nadu Trinamool Mahila Congress, said: "Mamataji has a clean image and she is very popular in our state, especially among women. We are waiting for her visit."

Heading: Missing children: panel wants FIRs to be made compulsory - Indian Express
Content:
In a new development in the Neeraj Grover murder case, sources in the Mumbai Police on Thursday said a top-level IPS officer, a retired deputy commissioner of police and a politician had called up the Malad police seeking an explanation from officers as to why Kannada movie actress Mariah Monica Susairaj was being grilled by them. This was before the Crime Branch announced that the case had been cracked.

"A serving officer of the rank of Additional Director General of Police, a retired DCP who was posted in the Local Arms division of the Mumbai Police and an important MNS politician had called Malad police station on May 8 and asked questions as to why Susairaj was being called to the police station and questioned," said an officer.

Susairaj and her naval officer boyfriend Emile Jerome Mathew were arrested by the Crime Branch on May 21 for their alleged roles in the May 7 murder of Neeraj Grover, a top executive at Synergy Adlabs and former creative head of Balaji Telefilms.

According to sources, investigators probing the murder suspect that Susairaj had reached out to an 'influential and well-connected' friend, who in turn contacted the two police officers and the politician to garner help for her.

Meanwhile, on Thursday, both Susairaj and Mathew were produced at the Esplanade Court, where the police secured their custody till June 3. Susairaj's brother Richard was present on the court premises.

On May 27, after she had expressed her desire to confess, Susairaj had been taken into judicial custody and her confessional statement was recorded for two days in front of a magistrate.

The Crime Branch has moved an application before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate who recorded her confession, seeking a copy of her statement under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

"We have moved an application to get a copy of Susairaj's confessional statement, and we are hoping to get it tomorrow," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

Heading: Not enough water? Manufacture some, says Israel - Indian Express
Content:
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is formulating a set of guidelines to make it mandatory for police stations to lodge First Information Reports regarding missing children. The NCPCR also wants police stations to have a separate register for complaints regarding missing children.

"Currently, the rule book in the police stations does not say that an FIR should be lodged for every child who goes missing. In most cases, the FIRs regarding missing children go missing themselves and thereby enable the police to easily wash off their hands," said Sandhya Bajaj, member of NCPCR. The NCPCR has been working on the guidelines for the past three months and has written to all the states to give reports regarding missing children. The guidelines will soon be sent to the Government for approval.

According to a recent survey, maximum children are reported missing from Ludhiana in Punjab. "We have received a number of complaints from parents of missing children from Punjab, particularly from Ludhiana. In such cases, parents are already traumatised; the police can help them by following up the cases and informing them regularly," added Bajaj.

While there is hardly any state that has made it mandatory for police stations to lodge FIRs regarding missing children, a few states have taken some steps towards addressing the issue, though the NCPCR says these are not enough.

FACTFILE

• In 2006, 3,649 children went missing in UP. Out of 61 children who were reported missing between April and December 2006 from UP, the Union Ministry of Women & Child Development could locate and send back 54 kids to their homes. Lucknow District Police found 300 out of 1,047 missing children in 2006.

•After 24 children were reported missing between July 2006 and January 2007 from a tribal area, Chhattisgarh formed a special squad to probe into such cases.

• According to Kolkata Police, 15,600 kids went missing from the city between 1996 and 2005.

Heading: India should aim to eliminate Type-1 polio virus by 2008 end, say experts - Indian Express
Content:
India could learn a thing or two from Israel when it comes to supplying municipal water to meet ever-rising demands. "Manufactured water" is probably the ideal solution, says Mo Provizor, director of the Israeli Water Authority.

Speaking to The Indian Express on the sidelines of WATECH 2008, an international conference on industrial and urban water management technologies, he said Israel currently meets about 25 per cent of its water needs with recycled sewage water and desalinated seawater and brackish water; it has hopes of upping the number to 50 per cent by 2013.

According to Provizor, it is feasible for India to use manufactured water to meet its demands at reasonable costs as well. "Desalination of seawater is not the only way to do this," he said, adding that Israel also uses a system that recycles wastewater after desalination.

"The recycled water can be used to replenish nearby aquifers on a regular basis. Later, this water can be pumped up to supply potable water to cities," he said, adding that this method is especially useful for landlocked places.

Citing the example of Israel, which is planning to set up three new desalination plants by private parties on a BOT basis, he said that extensive private participation would be essential to make a success out of a large-scale water manufacturing project.

However, he added that to make such a venture successful, the government should agree to share unforeseen costs.

Heading: Common minimum hike: Rs 1-2 for fuel, Rs 20 LPG - Indian Express
Content:
The India Expert Advisory Group (IEAG) on Polio has recommended that the Health Ministry should focus on eliminating Type-1 polio virus this year and prepare to eradicate Type-3 virus transmission by 2009. "India is leading an intensified polio eradication effort against Type-1 virus and has recorded the lowest ever transmission level of the virus since 2007 till date," said members of the expert group at their two-day meet which concluded on Thursday.

According to the Union Health Ministry, one of most vulnerable states — Uttar Pradesh — has not seen a single Type-1 case this year and Bihar has reported only one case as of now. "India can be the first country to eliminate Type-1 polio virus by 2008 end if speedy and large-scale mop-up vaccination rounds are carried out in response to fresh polio cases," said the experts.

The group advised the Health Ministry to focus on getting rid of Type-1 virus in Bihar. "All states should be on alert to quickly detect and rapidly respond to any new poliovirus case," it added.

According to Health Ministry officials, the Type-3 poliovirus outbreak in 2007 in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar has been curtailed to a great extent and has been declining rapidly.

Heading: To clear cop air, Maya asks for CBI to probe Arushi; says ‘grave’ electronic evidence - Indian Express
Content:
The government has, in principle, decided to increase prices of petrol by Rs 2 per litre, diesel by Re 1 per litre and cooking gas by Rs 20 per cylinder but will try and push for a higher raise at Saturday's Cabinet meeting.

Sources said that Petroleum Minister Murli Deora's proposal before the Cabinet would be an increase of Rs 3 per litre on petrol, Rs 2 on diesel and Rs 50 on a cooking gas cylinder so that in case allies protest — which they are likely to do, the Left has already opposed any hike — the internally approved price will be pushed as a compromise solution.

Sources said that Congress President and UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi also approved the price hike late evening at a meeting with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, Finance Minister P Chidambaram and Deora.

The proposed hike was arrived at by the ministers and the PM this afternoon when considering measures to bail out the cash-strapped state-run oil marketing companies that may lose Rs 225,000 crore during 2008-09 for selling transport and cooking fuels below cost, sources said.

"Some things have been agreed at today's meeting, but I cannot say what the Cabinet will decide," Deora said after the meeting with Mukherjee, Chidambaram, Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia and Prime Minister's Principal Secretary T K Nair.

After Deora and Chidambaram locked horns over the issue, the senior ministers opted for the usual three-pronged strategy where Deora would raise prices to fetch OMCs Rs 7,500 crore with Chidambaram contributing equally through a marginal cut in excise and customs duty on crude oil and petroleum products.

The OMCs would be asked to take a hit of Rs 45,000 crore with state-run oil producers chipping in Rs 30,000 crore to reduce the under-recoveries. The government would agree to bear the remaining Rs 90,000 crore as bonds in the hope that losses would pare to Rs 180,000 crore with decline in crude prices.

In the absence of an internal concurrence, the government decided to postpone a meeting of the Group of Ministers where members from Congress's ally parties would also have been present.

Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India made an exception in borrowing norms for the OMCs by allowing banks to lend up to 25 per cent of their exposure in a single sector. The present norm is that banks cannot lend more than 15 per cent in a single sector, with a leeway of 5 per cent more in special circumstances.

The ceiling was raised through a circular amending the Master Circular on Exposure Norms to help Hindustan Petroleum, Bharat Petroleum and Indian Oil, who are left with cash good for only meeting imports for two to three months. End-July, HPCL and BPCL would have exhausted their credit line and ended up without money to fund their business any longer.

Heading: Renuka stoops to attack: I think as a  mom, Maya as CM - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati today recommended that the Arushi murder case be handed over to the CBI, saying that while she believed the state police were doing their best, the victim's family believed otherwise.

Defending the UP Police, which has been accused of shoddy investigation, Mayawati said: "The police are serious about nabbing the accused and a few arrests have been made after questioning the family. Yet the victim's family is accusing the police of not investigating the case properly."

If the victim's family didn't have faith, the state government was ready to refer the case to the CBI, "provided the Central Government agrees to it", she said.

Late in the evening, the Uttar Pradesh Home Department sent a formal recommendation to the Department of Personnel, Government of India.

However, before the Mayawati government's request reached the Centre, Union Minister of State for Home Sriprakash Jaiswal told reporters that there was no need for a CBI inquiry when the UP Special Task Force was already probing the matter.

He added that a CBI investigation could only be ordered when a crime had multi-state links. "When the accused or crime is only one state specific, then I don't think a CBI probe is needed," Jaiswal said.

Accusing the Congress of politicising the case and having no sympathy for the victim's family, Mayawati told its leadership at the Centre to assist the state in finding the guilty. "Or else my ministers would be compelled to bring to light all those heinous crimes that take place quite frequently in Delhi and other Congress-ruled states," she said.

The Chief Minister also pointed out that the probe into the case — in which Arushi's father Dr Rajesh Talwar has been arrested — was not yet complete, but whatever facts have emerged the police have shared these with the media. "However, during the electronic investigation and electronic surveillance some evidence has surfaced that is of grave nature and propriety does not allow the police to share this with the media, though this evidence was produced before the court today."

Both the Congress and BJP said Mayawati's decision showed that she had no faith in her own police force. "She should state if she has lost confidence in her own police," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari told reporters here. He also dismissed as "mere rhetoric" Mayawati's allegations that the Centre was playing politics in the Arushi case.

BJP vice-president Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi said UP had been seeing a sort of "horror show" since Mayawati came to power.

Heading: At CPM central committee meeting, comrades show strong withdrawal symptoms - Indian Express
Content: Denying charge of politicising the Arushi case, Union Minister for Women and Child Development Renuka Chowdhury said on Thursday: "I am thinking like a mother, and Mayawati should not think only like a CM...It's a matter of concern that a young innocent girl is killed inside her house.'

Heading: Central genetic panel clears India’s own strain of Bt Cotton for the market - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM's newly elected Central Committee has told the party leadership to either make the Government perform or stop supporting it.

The general mood at the Central Committee (CC) was combative with members making it clear that the party's credibility would be at stake if it continues to support a "hugely unpopular UPA Government."

They told the leadership that they couldn't face an election with the present arrangement. Central Committee members felt that the Government had miserably failed in arresting price rise. They were of the view that the Government was more interested in the Indo-US nuclear deal than containing inflation.

Members from Bengal and Kerala said the party should take immediate steps to distance itself from the Congress. Most of the CC members from West Bengal said the Panchayat poll setback had something to do with the alliance with the Congress at the Centre.

A Central Committee member said that there was a consensus in the CC that it would be suicidal for the CPM to go to polls with the current arrangement. "When and on what issue we will withdraw support is yet to be finalised. But it has certainly been hotly debated in this CC," he said.

The Bengal group thinks much more than the nuclear deal, the rise in price of commodities and petrol is an issue on which the Left could serve ultimatum on the UPA. The Bengal group in the CC was not in favour of withdrawing support on the nuclear deal because it is a complex subject with no mass appeal.

•It will be difficult to explain to the common man the intricacies and the impact of the nuclear deal.

•There are basic differences within the Bengal group over the utility of nuclear power. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, for example, is in favour of nuclear power unlike hardliners such as Prakash Karat who are not only against the deal but against nuclear power as well.

CPM leader Mohammed Salim, when contacted, said that withdrawal of support from the UPA was not on the agenda but issues such as price rise were taken up for discussion. "We have urged the UPA government to initiate corrective steps on this issues. First we want to see how the UPA government responds. The next step will be decided after that," he said.

The decision-making body of the party today also discussed the party's West Bengal unit's report on the panchayat polls, in the wake of the losses it suffered in Nandigram and Singur.

While admitting that there was no need for reversing the government's industrialisation policy, the Central Committee was of the view that there were serious errors in the way the policy was implemented and sought "utmost care."

Quite in tune with the mood of the CC, the CPM today released in advance the editorial of the latest issue of People's Democracy which says that the UPA is losing political and electoral support because of growing popular discontent as it has failed to do justice to the CMP. "The Left's support to the UPA government, an expression of its consistent commitment to keep the communal combination away from power at the Centre, is based on the CMP. Pressures will be mounted for implementing its content, while popular struggles will be strengthened on every departure from the CMP. In its final year, this UPA government must redeem its promises made in the CMP," the editorial says.

Emerging out of the CC meeting, politburo member Sitaram Yechury said that there was a need to stop growing public discontent against the government and ensure that communal forces do not benefit from it. "The Karnataka verdict is a clear indication of the discontent due to price rise and continuing agrarian crisis," Yechury said.

Heading: Last year, national highway projects crawled the slowest ever - Indian Express
Content:
India's own Bt cotton is set for commercial release.

The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC), the apex body for granting clearances to genetically modified crops, in its meeting on May 2, granted permission for the commercial release of Bikaner Narma (BN) Bt variety, developed by Nagpur's Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), in the north, central and south regions. The CICR's Bt cotton is a variety and not a hybrid. So, the farmers will be able to replicate it on their farms rather than buy fresh seeds every season unlike the hybrids they have been buying ever since Bt cotton was allowed in the country.

Moreover, the CICR variety will be available at much cheaper rates to farmers.

In 2005, CICR scientists had successfully developed their own protocol (method) for a primary transgenic variety. Using what is called as as meristem culture, they had introduced the Cry1 Ac Bt gene in the famous Rajasthan variety called Bikaner Narma. The variety was tested for all requirements across the country. The scientists had also introduced the gene in three other varieties—LRA 1566, LRK 516 and RG 8 (Desi cotton). These are still under trials in various parts of the country.

When contacted, GEAC co-chairman C D Mayee told The Indian Express: "The CICR effort was on for several years and this is for the first time in the country that a variety is being released. It will be available at a low price and the farmers will be able to replicate it themselves."

But with the latest cotton season just a few days ahead, the seeds of the new variety will be available to farmers only the next season. CICR acting Director Keshav Kranthi said the CICR will now start production of the seeds and will try to make it available to a large number of farmers by next season.

Heading: Honour killings don’t happen in families like ours, says mother - Indian Express
Content:
The country's biggest infrastructure upgrade under the National Highways Development Programme (NHDP) has recorded the lowest-ever progress rate under this government in 2007-08.

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has posted a 56 per cent project completion rate across all phases of the NHDP in 2007-08 in terms of completion of projects — the lowest since the UPA came to power and Union Minister T R Baalu came to head the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways.

The NHDP exercise is on along 33,000 km of national highways across NHDP I, II, III and V.

It has only been a slide down in the NHDP progress rate since 2004 and that was evident earlier this week when Baalu held a review with NHAI. Consider these:

•Project completion rate was 81 per cent in 2004-05, 78 per cent in 2006-07, 73 per cent in 2005-06 and is now down to 56 per cent.

• Project award rate is down from 70 per cent in 2005-06 to 17 per cent in 2007-08.

• 2007-08 has seen one of the worst ever performances by NHAI with only 1,614 km upgraded against a target of 2,885 km.

•NHDP I and II together have registered a 50% progress against the target in terms of completion of length in 2007-08.

•NHDP I and II, which include the Golden Quadrilateral and North South East West corridor, have been very slow. As many as 22 contracts along 177 km on the GQ are still pending. Ten of these are even likely to go beyond the latest deadline of June 2008.

• Another 72 km on the North South East West corridor and 184 km of port-connectivity projects are yet to take off while several NHDP II projects are yet to be awarded.

While the PM-chaired Committee on Infrastructure (CoI) expressed acute dissatisfaction with NHAI's progress in its review meeting in December 2007, the picture was equally dismal during the Planning Commission's re-check with NHAI last month.

The Plan panel pointed out that NHAI was taking 20 months on an average to award a project against the set timeframe of five months.

Incidentally, while projects move along sluggishly, there is no slowdown in the investment being pumped into the NHDP.

NHAI spent Rs 15,639 crore on NHDP in 2007-08 — 89 per cent of what was allocated — and has been fairly close to the expenditure target in the last four years.

NHAI has argued that the slowdown is because the government is yet to notify and approve the new toll rules and the Model Concession Agreements (MCA) for the toll. It also pointed out that the government's rules on shortlisting, evaluation and verification of Request for Quotation (RFQ) documents are delaying the award of projects.

Added to this, NHAI claims, is the dearth of technical and financial staff, shortage of raw materials for contractors, overall shortage of skilled manpower in the industry. And that the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) on which the toll is decided does not fully reflect market conditions.
