Other participating Indian institutes include the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune, Birbal Sahani Institute, Lucknow, Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, Dehra Dun, Agarkar Research Institute, Pune, IIT Roorkie and Pune and Punjab University.

The project will also study lakes in the Himalayas and also in Germany. "We will try and evolve a model based on the study to predict future climatic changes, which is very important since climatic changes, drought and flood cycles are now intensifying," said Prasad.

Heading: Nanded farmers turn shareholders in realty venture - Indian Express
Content:
The Guardian

A report on the Gurjjar blockade explains the issue in the context of reservations. The Indian government, it says, runs the world's largest affirmative action programme by reserving 50 per cent of government jobs and university places for those who suffered for centuries under caste oppression. The problem with the Gurjjar community, it adds, is that the British labelled them a criminal tribe, and though the Indian establishment calls them backward, they feel they are not considered "backward enough" to reap the full benefits of reservations. The report cites historians who debate on the relative injustice perpetrated on the community by the British and by the caste system. It ends with the words of those who feel that the Gurjjar case highlights the dangers of caste-based reservations and that "succumbing to the Gurjjars' demands would simply lead to a race to the bottom".

The Economist

This report from Raipur is an indictment of the Indian Union and the Chhattisgarh state government's laws against Maoists. The story begins with the plight of Dr Binayak Sen, the PUCL activist who has spent more than a year in jail and whose trial began in April. While the report mentions the violence the Maoists periodically show themselves capable of, it criticises the Indian penal code and the draconian Chhattisgarh Special Public Security Act for meting out inhuman treatment—Sen was allegedly guilty of passing on letters from a jailed Maoist. The Economist also takes the state government to task for relying on vigilante groups without doing much for public security. The state is not likely to win the case against Sen, with his cause having been taken up by 22 Nobel laureates. In fact, the Special Public Security Act is now backfiring on the government.

The New York Times

The quality of healthcare in India is often dependent on the position that you occupy in the social ladder, says an article in The New York Times. The poor, like the victims of the recent hooch tragedy, usually end up with caregivers who are incompetent, ill-trained or indifferent to their needs, while private hospitals pamper foreigners flocking to avail medical facilities that cost a fraction of what they might in a country like the United States.

Heading: HC slams VS Govt’s move to take over Trivandrum Golf Club - Indian Express
Content:
Eighty-four-year-old Damodhar Dugane has lived his entire life growing vegetables, mangoes, guava and sugarcane — just like generations before him have done. The patriarch, who owns 10 acres of land along with his brother, is today a shareholder in a real estate company: A company of which he is as much a part as 250 other families from Nanded village in Pune.

Reams have been written about the entrepreneurship of a bunch of 120 farmers, headed by Satish Magar, the brainchild behind the Magarpatta city township in Pune. Now, more than 20 km away, another group of farmers have sown the seeds of yet another success story. Together, they have pooled in their land to create a 700-acre canvas for the Nanded city township at Pune-Sinhgad road.

With the vagaries of time making agriculture an unprofitable business, these farmers have decided that the mushrooming of towering structures on their land is a much better proposition. "However, we didn't want to follow the example of those farmers who sell off their plots to developers on a one-time payment, leaving them with no other source of income," said Bharat Dangude, a farmer who has booked a two-bedroom flat in the new township.

Soon, they met Satish Magar, the chief promoter of Magarpatta city, who decided to replicate his model township in Nanded village. "Coming from an agricultural background myself, I knew most of the farmers. We discussed the idea for two years before launching the project," he said.

Unlike other real estate projects that thrive on private equities and foreign investment, this one will be executed with the help of money generated by the company and farmers.

The Magarpatta Township Development and Construction Company will hold a 51 per cent stake in the new venture.

The rest of the stakes will be distributed in proportion to their holdings among the farmers who own as little as half-an-acre to 100 acres each.

"Over the last 10 years, with the city edging closer to our farms, the production has gone down miserably. In addition to the pollution from the city affecting our produce, there has been a dearth of labourers, as everyone wants to work in the city where they earn much more. Even our children prefer going to cities in search of a livelihood," said Dugane.

"Mango and sugarcane production have been hit so badly that that we can hardly hope to recover our costs," said Maruti Dhawade, another farmer who owns one-acre land and runs a subsidiary construction business on a small scale. Today, Dhawane has purchased a 20-acre land with the token amount of Rs 5 lakh that he received for his smallholding. He has also been awarded the contract for constructing the boundary wall at the project site.

Damodhar Dugane's 52-year-old son, who used to help him in the fields, will start a nursery that will provide plants for landscaping the township. Like them, the second generation of all locals here will be involved in various works that goes into creating a township, like canteen facilities, constructing roads, stone quarrying and transportation.

On Sunday, as the foundation stone for the project was laid by the Chief Minister, the farmers expressed little apprehension about the fact that the land that once sprouted sugarcanes will now sport apartments, bungalows, gymnasiums, joggers park, riverside resorts, eco parks and adventure park, malls, theme restaurants.

Employments hubs will include IT parks, gaming and animation centres. The commercial spaces would not be sold, but rented out so that it becomes a constant stream of revenue for the farmers as well as the company.

Heading: Karnataka stonewalls Hogenakkal project - Indian Express
Content:
The Kerala High Court on Monday slammed the state Government for bulldozing norms and procedures to take over one of India's oldest golf clubs in Thiruvananthapuram. The court termed the move anti-democratic, and asked the Government to return the club to its owners forthwith.

The court also asked the state Revenue Secretary who had issued the takeover order even as the HC was considering a petition against it, to appear before it next week. Justice Sirijagan, who heard the petitioners, observed that the official had shown disrespect to the court.

The Left Government had sealed and taken over the 125-year-old Trivandrum Golf Club on Tuesday morning, on the ground that the club owed it some Rs 56 crore in land rent arrears.

This, the Government held, meant that the club's 25.38 acres that the Government leased it in 1962 could be seized. The club held up a 2006 Government ruling that said the land deal was a licence agreement and not a lease arrangement, and the club did not owe the Government land rent arrears.

While the HC asked the Government on Monday to explain the hurry to push through this premium club's takeover, Government sources said the idea was to convert the club into a 'culture complex'. Just before the court axed the move, state Sports Minister M Vijayakumar had stated that the Cabinet had decided to push for the takeover and had even formed a four-member ministerial sub-committee to take the idea forward.

This committee of ministers, Vijayakumar claimed, would look at how the club could be used for improving the game of golf in Kerala, and make the club which has about 500 members, mostly politicians and bureaucrats, into a 'people's club'. The minister had stressed that the club would be made to provide access to all who want to play Golf, and not limit the facilities to an exclusive class.

Chief Minister V S Achuthanandan said soon after the court pronounced the order that his Government would now appeal against it.

Heading: TN restaurants to reduce prices on CM b’day - Indian Express
Content:
Signalling a tough stand on the Hogenakkal issue on which both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are at loggerheads, Karnataka Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa on Monday said every effort would be made to safeguard the interests of his state.

"Interests of the people of Karnataka is very important to me and every attempt will be made to safeguard the interests of the state," he said at a press conference here when asked about Tamil Nadu's drinking water project, which he opposed in the run up to the polls. Noting he had already discussed the issue with irrigation and legal experts, Yeddyurappa said an all party leaders' meeting would be convened soon after the vote of confidence this week to discuss the issue. The Chief Minister said that protection of land, water resources, borders, language and culture of Karnataka was of utmost importance and "there is no scope for compromise in this regard".

Asked whether he would meet M Karunanidhi on the issue, he said he would like to meet everybody. He said there was a need for the Centre and the Chief Ministers of both the states to sit across the table and discuss the issue.

Heading: Sons’ rise stalled, patriarch stays unelected for 10th time - Indian Express
Content:
As promised to the Tamil Nadu Government earlier, restaurants in the state would reduce prices of popular delicacies from Tuesday onwards, which also coincides with the 85th birthday of Chief Minister M Karunanidhi.

At a meeting with State Food Minister E V Velu here, representatives of the Hotel Owners' Association resolved to reduce the prices of idli, dosa, vada, pongal and tea by about 10 to 15 per cent. These food items are priced between Rs 8 to Rs 15, the release said adding that the members agreed to display the revised rates in their respective eateries.

Heading: Karunanidhi to press for project, says call it ‘Sethuram' - Indian Express
Content:
Ending days of speculation regarding the imminent rise of the sons of DMK patriarch and Chief Minister M Karunanidhi into the top echelons of the party, the general council that met here on Monday decided to continue with the present leadership at all levels, till the organisational polls are completed by the end of the year. In the process, the party has — inadvertently — delayed the re-election of Karunanidhi, the incumbent president, for the 10th time consecutively. He has been leading the party since former CM Annadurai's death in 1969.

In the run-up to the council meeting, the highest policy making body of the party, rumours were rife that both M K Stalin and M K Azhagiri would be given "additional responsibilities" a euphemism for them assuming greater powers in the state Government and the party.

Stalin, the local administration minister and deputy general secretary of the party in-charge of the youth wing, was stated to be elevated as the deputy chief minister, another euphemism for CM-in-waiting. Azhagiri, on the other hand, who has little mass appeal unlike his younger brother, was expected to be made vice-president — a non-existent post said to be created only to accommodate the ill-tempered son.

These posts would have made them second only to their father in both the state Government and party. However, the inner-party elections could not be completed due to 'natural calamities like rains and floods', maintained the party, deferring decisions on this regard till the elections were completed.

Sources in the party said some of the members, including a former MLA, raised the issue of continuing attack from alliance partner PMK and its leader S Ramadoss on the state Government and party. There were demands of expelling them from the alliance, said a source.

The general council, comprising ministers, district and state level office-bearers, that met on Monday at the party headquarters, Anna Arivalayam, demanded a constitutional amendment to empower the state Government to fix the total quantum of reservation as per the ground realities. The Supreme Court had stayed a law brought in by the DMK Government envisaging 69 per cent reservation to OBCs, pointed out the resolution as the need for this demand.

The party reiterated its line of reservation for all OBC members, instead of omitting the rich among them from the quota basket. The DMK demanded reservation in the private sector, if the needy were to avail the full benefits of social justice.

Apart from the OBCs, the party is also in favour of reservation for Muslims and Christians at the national level.

Heading: First word from Spain, assures Jamal Khan’s wife of fair treatment - Indian Express
Content:
DMK patriarch and Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, who had antagonised Hindu organisations, spearheading protests against dredging through Ram Sethu, with his comments on Lord Ram, penned a reconciliatory poem in his column in the party mouthpiece Murasoli on Sunday. In his poem, Karunanidhi — who would turn 85 on Tuesday — said he was ready to rename SSCP as 'Sethuram project' if that would clear the hurdles pertaining to the completion of Sethusamudram Shipping Canal Project. However, on Monday Karunanidhi indicated that only the words have changed, not his dream. Addressing 1,500 members of the DMK general council here, he said the party should be ready to launch a massive agitation for the speedy completion of the controversial project, whether in power or out of it.

Party observers pointed out that this could be a reference to the Supreme Court observation, warning dismissal of the state Government, after Tamil Nadu came to a standstill during a bandh on October 1 last, over the project. The mode and timing of the agitation would be decided later, said sources, though office bearers refused to comment on it. The general council meeting was out of bounds for the media.

Pointing out that the project was a 150-year-old dream of the Tamilians, including many past chief ministers like C N Annadurai and K Kamaraj, Karunanidhi said the completion of the project was a 'historic necessity' for the prosperity of the state.

The atheist leader had earlier antagonised a large section of Hindus by questioning the very existence of Ram. If the earlier outburst against Ram was charged with his angst regarding staunch opposition and subsequent delay in completing the controversial project, his poem was charged emotionally, but this time by the "quiver in his voice" as the octogenarian wrote. Through the piece he urged everyone — including the BJP — not to scuttle the project in the name of Ram.

In fact, through his poem, the CM sought to differentiate between religion and development, and more importantly, between faith and politics. However, as his exhortation proves, only the wordage was changed to soothe ruffled feathers, and not the intention to go ahead with the project in full steam. The general council, the highest policy making body of the party, adopted a resolution urging the Centre to complete the project as soon as possible.

Heading: Arushi murder: Renuka plans defamation suit against cops - Indian Express
Content:
In the first official communication since Mumbai resident Roshan Jamal Khan was arrested in connection with an alleged terror plot in Spain more than four months ago, the Spanish Consulate has written to his wife assuring that her husband would be treated fairly under Spanish law.

But that has not brought much relief to the anxious family as it has learnt that the lawyer representing him in Madrid died last week.

Khan was among 14 Muslim men picked up by Spanish authorities from a mosque in Barcelona on January 19 in connection with an alleged plot to carry out terror attacks in the city. Four of them, including another Indian, were released later. Khan, who is being held along with nine Pakistanis, was in Spain to explore the possibility of starting an olive business, his family has said.

In a letter dated May 29 addressed to Khan's wife Farida, a copy of which is with The Indian Express, Cesar Alba, the Consul-General of Spain in Mumbai, has "guaranteed" fair treatment for Khan and a chance to furnish evidence of his innocence.

"The guarantee offered by our legal system is absolute and you can have complete confidence in the Spanish judicial system, which is based on the principles of independence, responsibility and subjection of the rule of law," Alba said in the letter. "The judicial process... will permit Mr Khan to present all the necessary evidence in his favour."

Elaborating on the reason behind Khan's detention, Alba said that he was detained under Operation 'Cantata'. 'Cantata' roughly translates as 'singing', a term often used by police to describe an informant spilling the beans on his accomplices. "Mr Khan is in prison awaiting judgement for a crime of integrating with a terrorist organisation and of illegal possession of explosives," the diplomat added.

Speaking to The Indian Express from Madrid, Khan's brother-in-law Amanullah said: "Last Wednesday, Sebastian Sallelas, the lawyer representing Roshan, passed away. This is another blow for us. No date for a court appearance has been set even now."

"We came to know from my uncle that my father's lawyer has passed away a few days ago. Now we do not know who is representing him. I just hope this does not affect the case, and lead to further delays," said Khan's son Tanha (16).

Heading: Meghalaya at Centre door as Assam claims hill village - Indian Express
Content:
Not satisfied with the transfer of police officials who used derogatory language for the murdered teenaged girl Arushi, the Union Women and Child Development Ministry in a meeting on Monday examined legal options for initiating action against the police officers. The options explored by the ministry include a defamation case against the officials as well as provisions within the Juvenile Justice Act.

"I don't think the action taken was sufficient. In fact, this is no action," said Union Women and Child Development Minister Renuka Chowdhury after the meeting. Chowdhury headed the meeting of members of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), Law Ministry officials, lawyers, and members of various NGOs.

"The idea is not to pull down the administration but to set an example so that such things are not repeated. There is enough legislation regarding this and we are examining the options," sources in the ministry said. The officials will meet again on Thursday to decide on the action to be taken against the cops. Chowdhury will also have discussions with I&B Ministry on the way media handled the issue.

Responding to Mayawati's charge that the murder case is being politicised, Chowdhury said: "Mayawati is thinking like a Chief Minister, I am thinking like a mother. There is a difference between the two. If Mayawati feels it is okay to talk about a 14-year-old girl in such derogatory terms in public and the girl is defamed after her death, then it is unfortunate indeed."

"Such cases should be treated with sensitivity. We expect the police to have undergone training in this regard and are hence, outraged to hear such comments made by police officials even before the probe is complete. This is a violation of law," Chowdhury added.

The NCPCR had sent a notice to the police officials asking for an explanation. The organisation is yet to get a response. "If they do not respond within a stipulated time, we will take action against them," said a member of the NCPCR.

Heading: Indian duo on death row in China granted consular access - Indian Express
Content:
Assam and Meghalaya have landed in a fresh dispute over their common border, with the latter moving the Centre and seeking intervention of New Delhi to stop Assam from encroaching upon its territory. Trouble began last Friday when Assam Health Minister Himanta Biswa Sharma announced plans to set up a health centre at a village called Lampi (Langpih according to Meghalaya) in Kamrup district on the inter-state border. According to Meghalaya, Langpih is in West Khasi Hills district and comprises 74 villages of Garos and Khasis that fall under Rambrai Syiemship (chiefdom).

Soon after Sharma laid the foundation stone of the health centre on Saturday, Meghalaya Chief Minister Donkupar Roy and Deputy Chief Minister Hopingstone Lyngdoh — who also holds the home portfolio — had a meeting on Monday to discuss the issue. Incidentally, Langpih falls under Lyngdoh's constituency. Roy told reporters after the meeting: "We have no other option but to approach the Union Government or the Supreme Court to settle issue."

Refuting allegation that Meghalaya was being soft on Assam, Roy said: "We do not want to wage a war, but let me assure you we are not going soft either. Constitutionally and by way of official documents, the land belongs to Meghalaya."

Earlier, Roy had called up Union Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta and lodged a complaint against Assam of "illegally occupying" its land. The Meghalaya Government had also sent an official letter to the Assam Government asking it to stop any visit by Sharma to the village, with Meghalaya official spokesman Paul Lyngdoh asserting that the village belonged to the hill state and not Assam.

Assam, however, chose to ignore Meghalaya's plea with Sharma going ahead with the foundation stone laying ceremony. This despite the fact that Meghalaya had tried to prevent Sharma from making it to the place by blocking the road to the village with felled trees and other barriers.

"Lampi belongs to Assam. We have got a border police outpost there for several decades. If Meghalaya has any problem, it can approach the Centre or the Supreme Court," Sharma said.

Assam has accused Meghalaya of encroaching upon 5473.92 hectares of its land since the hill state was carved out of two districts — the United Khasi and Jaintia Hills, and Garo Hills — in 1972 when Indira Gandhi went for reorganisation of the northeastern region. Assam Revenue Minister Bhumidhar Barman said Meghalaya has encroached upon 3.2 hectares of land in Kamrup district since 1975, apart from 42.08 hectares in Kamrup (Metro) district since 1975.

Meghalaya, on the other hand, has accused Assam of encroaching upon 40 sq km of its territory since 1979 in West Khasi Hills district. "Assam had also set up polling booths inside our territory during elections," Lyngdoh said.

Blaming successive Meghalaya governments since 1979 of neglecting the issue, Roy on Monday appealed to all political parties, especially the Congress, not to politicise the issue and help resolving it. He said: "We will continue our effort to resolve the issue through dialogue even as we approach either the Centre of Supreme Court."

Heading: Former Bihar minister, son get life term for murder - Indian Express
Content:
Two Indians facing the firing squad after being convicted of smuggling narcotics by a Chinese court have been granted consular access.

Aksar Miyan and Hussain Mydeen, both hailing from Tamil Nadu, were handed down the death sentence by the Intermediate People's Court in Zhuohai in August last year.

"We have received today an intimation from the High People's Court of Guangdong province that an official can meet both on June 6," sources at the Indian consulate said.

An official from the Indian Consulate General of India in Gaungzhou would meet both Aksar and Hussain and "take their statements," sources said.

The Consulate had been pursuing the matter on a regular basis to get consular access after the Ministry of External Affairs sent the "papers", the sources said, adding that "we were working on it".

The Ministry of External Affairs action followed a plea by the family of Aksar to plead for commutation of his death sentence to "any kind of jail term".

"The consular access to both has been given. The Consulate official will meet both," the sources added.

Aksar and Hussain were arrested in separate cases in different provinces on charge of smuggling drugs to China last year.

Heading: Congmen see little wisdom in new panel - Indian Express
Content:
Former Bihar minister Aditya Singh and his son were sentenced to life imprisonment by a fasttrack court here in connection with an eight-year-old murder case.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Vijay Shanker Pathak, who had on May 30 convicted Singh and his son Suman of the murder of a brick kiln manager Ashok Singh, sentenced them to life imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 each. The father-son duo was alleged to have shot dead Ashok Singh and injured a clerk Ratan Singh at Gausa village in Nawada district on February 26, 2000.

Aditya Singh, who was then minister of state for animal husbandry in the Rabri Devi Government, was elected to the legislative Assembly six times from Hisua seat in Nawada district in the past on Congress ticket, and also as an Independent.

Earlier this year he was awarded similar punishment by a trial court for the murder of Lalan Singh, head of Sakarpur panchayat. Singh had challenged his conviction in the High Court and was on bail before being convicted once again in connection with the murder of Ashok Singh.

Heading: RSP withdraws from UPA-Left Coordination Committee - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress Working Committee's decision on Saturday to set up a committee to outline the roadmap for the party ahead of crucial Assembly and general elections has raised several eyebrows in the ruling party as a section of Congress leaders believe it is yet another exercise in tokenism with reports of several other committees, constituted in the past, still gathering dust.

Party sources also questioned the relevance of the new committee, to be appointed by party president Sonia Gandhi, given the fact that the high-powered Group to Look into Future Challenges was set to finalise its report on intra-party reforms at its next meeting on Tuesday after about eight months of deliberations.

Following the party's defeat in 1999 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress president had constituted an 11-member committee headed by A K Antony to look into the causes of the defeat and suggest remedial measures. Nobody knows what happened to Antony committee report, said sources.

Pranab Mukherjee committee had been appointed to look into the debacle in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh Assembly elections in 2003 and create a roadmap for 2004 Lok Sabha polls. Not much is known about what follow-up action was taken on Mukherjee committee report. Much before that, in 1998, P A Sangma committee was constituted to revitalise the party. Its report is also gathering dust.

"You cannot even recall off hand how many committees had been constituted in the past — Antony committee, Sangma committee, Manmohan Singh committee, K Karunakaran committee, Mukherjee committee, et al. Nobody remembers what happened to those reports and what follow-up action was taken. Now we have yet another committee. You cannot have such a knee-jerk bureaucratic approach to elections," said a senior Congress leader.

Meanwhile, the Congress is also set to hold yet another chintan shivir (brainstorming session) of the AICC to deliberate over the party's strategy in the forthcoming elections. It will be on the lines of the Pachmarhi session in 1998 and in Shimla in 2003. The next chintan shivir is likely to be held this month only, although its date and venue is yet to be decided, said the sources.

The suggestion to set up a new committee to suggest a roadmap for ensuing assembly and general elections had come from HRD Minister Arjun Singh and was accepted by the Congress President at the CWC meeting last Saturday. The committee has to submit its report in 15 days.

Heading: CPM feels the pressure - Indian Express
Content:
While its big brothers in the Left Front are still dithering on the issue of support to the UPA Government, the junior most partner in the front, the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP), has announced its decision to withdraw from the UPA-Left co-ordination committee as "a warning signal to the UPA Government".

The RSP, which is a part of the Marxist-led Governments in West Bengal and Kerala, and has three members in the Lok Sabha, took the decision after a meeting of its central committee here. "We are not happy with the UPA's economic policies and the Government is not changing its position despite our opposition. This has forced us to withdraw from the UPA-Left coordination committee," senior party leader Abani Roy said.

Party general secretary Chandrachoodan said that there is no point in continuing the support to an "anti-people" Government which is least bothered about the distress and troubles of the common man. "The Congress lost the recent elections as a fall out of its wrong policies, but it is not ready to learn a lesson from that," Chandrachoodan said. However, the RSP will continue to be a member of the UPA-Left co-ordination committee on Indo-US nuclear deal. Explaining party's decision, Chandrachoodan said that it is very much clear that the Congress cares least about the recommendations of the Left. "Earlier, they used to consult us. Now they don't even do that," he said, adding that this is their first salvo against the Government.

According to him, the RSP has taken this decision without consulting other Left parties. "We will be taking up the issue of withdrawing support to the UPA Government with other Left parties," he said. The RSP is also planning to organise a Left conclave in August with an attempt "to form the real third front".

Senior RSP leader Manoj Bhattacharjee said, "We are not entering into a debate over who among us is close to the Congress. We, as a Left party, cannot allow the Congress to serve the interest of the capitalist. We cannot be a part of the failures of UPA Government's economic policies which were designed against the poor."

Meanwhile, the other Left parties expressed unhappiness over the RSP's unilateral decision. "The UPA-Left co-ordination committee had been dysfunctional for quite some time. RSP's decision is its own. We are not a part of it," said a CPI(M) politburo member.

CPI's state secretary Manjukumar Majumder said, "The RSP has withdrawn from the UPA-Left co-ordination committee, but it is still a member of the Left co-ordination committee, consisting of four Left parties. It should have discussed with other Left parties before taking the decision."

Forward Bloc leader Hafiz Alam Sairani said, "Before making their decision public, I cannot understand why the RSP did not talk to us or the other Left parties. We too are fighting against the policies of the UPA Government."

Senior RSP leader and Bengal PWD Minister Kshiti Goswami said, "We have taken this decision after a detailed discussion. We have requested all Left Front partners, including the CPI(M) to join us. But it is for them to take the decision."

"Before taking the decision, we assessed issues like the Indo-US nuclear deal and inflation which became a burden for the people," added Goswami.

Heading: Rahul T20 live on DD, Cong bats it’s unlike ‘capitalist’ IPL - Indian Express
Content:
The RSP's withdrawal from the UPA-Left co-ordination committee has now put pressure on big brother CPI(M) to make its long-standing threat of pulling out of the Government real for the first time.

For the CPI(M), post panchayat polls debacle, it is important to keep the Left Front partners together, especially the RSP. Since March 14, 2007, when 14 villagers were killed in Nandigram police firing, the rift between the RSP and the CPI(M) has widened. The RSP has blamed the CPI(M) of favouring capitalists in Bengal by using the state Government to protect their interest.

Left Front chairman and CPI(M) state secretary Biman Bose said, "For the past two years, there has been no meetings of the UPA -Left coordination committee. Their decision to withdraw from the committee does not matter."

Heading: Amethi match: Rahul man of the moment - Indian Express
Content:
Dubbing the recent IPL cricket tournament as "capitalist", the Congress sought to defend the live telecast of Rajiv Gandhi Rural Cricket tournament final in Amethi by DD Sports on Monday saying a national broadcaster was "obliged" to show it.

The final match of the Twenty-20 rural cricket tournament in Amethi was watched by members of the Nehru-Gandhi family, including Amethi MP Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Vadra and Robert Vadra. Asked if DD Sports telecast it live because of the involvement of the Nehru-Gandhi family, AICC spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi said he felt "sorry" that the question came when it related to rural areas, whereas there was no question being asked when private TV channels showed IPL matches the entire day.

"Private channels show sports which involve lakhs and crores and are played by capitalist IPL, but they are not interested in any rural sports," Singhvi told reporters here.

Heading: MP minister quits after raids in ‘fake drug purchase’ - Indian Express
Content:
As Sachin Tendulkar, R P Singh and India A cricketer Pankaj Singh turned up for the Twenty20 Rajiv Gandhi Rural Cricket Tournament final on Monday, Rahul Gandhi was the clear winner of the day.

The Amethi MP's constituency couldn't stop thanking him for bringing the stars in their midst. "I touched Sachin's feet. I never imagined that a day would come when I would see Sachin personally. Rahul bhaiya has really given an unmatched gift on this occasion," said Tilak Singh, one of the players of the Sangrampur team.

Nilesh Kumar, the Man of the Match winner, called it "the golden moment" of his life. "Sachin's presence increased my josh on the ground," he exclaimed.

Rahul couldn't have hoped for a better way to win over the local youth, which he has always claimed to be his agenda. The tournament was organised by the Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust.

Many local cricketers hoped that the match would prove a launch pad to the big league, with an eye on local lad R P Singh.

BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla pointed out that a few selectors of UP Cricket Association were also present for the match. "I told them to consider the village boys who played in the tournament," he said.

"My job was to make available an opportunity to young village boys. They aspired to meet cricket star Sachin Tendulkar. More than 1,800 teams participated and around 30,000 young village boys played in this tournament," Rahul told reporters at the end of the tournament.

He added that while he desired to organise rural sports like kabaddi and volley ball, "the general mood was in favour of cricket".

Rahul also promised that the tournament would continue. "We have not decided yet whether it would be held after one or two years. Lekin ye aakhri nahin hai (But this is not the last time)," he replied to a question.

The MP emphasised that the event should not be linked to politics.

The tournament winner was the Rajpoot Cricket Club, Amethi, which got a cheque of Rs 3 lakh from Tendulkar.

Heading: Patil assures investors of full security in Naxal-hit  regions - Indian Express
Content:
Madhya Pradesh Health Minister Ajay Vishnoi, whose department has come under a cloud with the I-T department carrying out searches on premises owned by health officials twice in less than one year, resigned on Monday amid reports that he was asked to quit by the party high command.

After raids at his brother Abhay Vishnoi's premises on Friday, the Opposition clamoured for his head but the minister put up a brave front saying the operation was undertaken to defame him.

The minister's younger brother was brought on deputation from the energy department to Laghu Udyog Nigam, a government body entrusted with purchasing drugs and medical equipment. The minister and his brother have a joint property in Jabalpur, which was raided last week.

Vishnoi claimed he was innocent but was tendering his resignation because the allegations were "bringing a bad name" to the government. He claimed the party and the chief minister backed him but he was resigning on "moral grounds."

The minister was on the Opposition's target both for alleged irregularities in purchase of drugs and medicines and for proliferation of medical and nursery institutions during his tenure.

After Friday's raids, IAS officer Rajesh Rajora had also resigned on moral grounds. The 1990 batch officer was Health Commissioner when the scandal in the health department came to light. He was made Home Secretary a few months ago.

IT officials have alleged a link between health officials, builders and drug suppliers indicating that fake purchases were made and the money used to invest in properties. According to documents seized in Jabalpur, crores were paid to the government officials as commission. Irregularities in the operation of mobile dispensaries that take health services to rural areas have come to light.

Friday's raids came after last year's search and seizure operation by the I-T department on the premises of then director (health services) Dr Yogiraj Sharma, who was compulsorily retired by the government in the wake of reports that he had amassed properties.

Director (investigations) A K Singh on Monday confirmed that properties and valuables owned by Sharma and his accomplices ran into more than Rs 100 crore. Sharma alone owned more than 20 properties and accounted for a major share of the seizure.

Cash was stashed everywhere in his palatial houses in Bhopal's Shaktinagar locality, officials said. His accomplices included two drug manufacturers and a builder.

Among those raided last week included a retired IAS officer, newspaper owner-cum-builder, the Bhopal resident editor of his newspaper, the journalist's Indore-based brother, health department officials and builders. In all, 56 premises were covered under the search and survey operation that lasted for two days.

Those covered in the latest round have surrendered details of properties worth Rs 87.12 lakh. Cash and jewellery worth Rs 85.48 lakh was also seized during the searches. IT sources said 27 lockers, including five in Jabalpur, ten in Indore and five in Bhopal, were yet to be opened. Though not much investment was made in Rajora's name, authorities said lot of property was purchased in his father and in-laws' names.

Ministers under cloud

• Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan is accused of favouring a business conglomerate and getting paid in kind. Dumper trucks purchased in his wife's name were rented out to the company. The vehicles have since been sold to the company but an FIR has been lodged against Chouhan on the direction of a local court.

•PWD and IT Minister Kailash Vijayvargiya is facing a host of corruption charges. A CAG report had stated that scores of crores were fraudulently spent on works executed for Simhast Mela in 2004. Vijayvargiya was in-charge of Simhast mela. Another scam related to him took place when he was Indore mayor. Pension worth crores was 'distributed' among beneficiaries who did not exist.

•Revenue Minister Kamal Patel is under shadow for amassing properties running into tens of crores of rupees in and around Harda district.

• PHE minister Chaudhary Chandrabhan Singh has been accused of misusing his position to purchase land and other properties in and around Chhindwara, his constituency.

•Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Gopal Bhargava equated those seeking reservation with 'beggars.'

Heading: Act as a govt does on foreign policy, don’t pass buck: BJP tells UPA - Indian Express
Content:
Addressing the concerns of the industries on law and order situation, Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Monday said that the Government would ensure adequate security for industrial units even in the Naxal-affected areas and asked entrepreneurs to invest in such areas too.

In keeping with his often repeated line that wholesome development of the Naxal-hit areas was the only answer to naxalism, Patil said both the Centre as well as state Governments were committed to ensure that investments made by the industry are safe. "The Government is doing everything necessary to see that economic development takes place and allowing everybody to put in his efforts for the purpose," the Home Minister said at the 7th annual session of the ASSOCHAM.

He said despite isolated incidents of terrorism, the overall security situation had improved in most parts of the country. "Trends and statistics available indicate that the situation has not deteriorated, but improved in certain areas and parts of the country. Incidents that occur are highlighted. They create scare," Patil said, adding, "But, if we consider the trends, they appear to be encouraging."

"The information and our assessment of the situation do indicate to us that the situation can be controlled, is under control, will be better controlled, despite a few tragic incidents that appear to be happening at places," he said.

Calling on the industry to become partners in India's development, Patil said, "The increase in production and growth is bound to help the people."

Heading: Yeddyurappa to replicate Gujarat ‘growth story’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi, in an interview with The Indian Express, asked the UPA Government to present "more facts" on the Indo-US nuclear deal, the BJP asked the Congress to "take a clear stand on the issue instead of blaming others".

"Why do they blame either their partners or the Opposition? It is for the Congress to arrive at a solution," senior leader Jaswant Singh said, speaking on the foreign policy resolution adopted at the party's National Executive here.

Asked whether the BJP was egging on the Government to go ahead with the nuclear deal, Singh said: "It is not a question of egging. Take responsibility as a government. No government is obliged to seek parliamentary approval."

The resolution slammed the UPA Government for "dereliction of duty" in addressing foreign policy concerns and accused it of abdicating its responsibility "by outsourcing its foreign and security policies to the Communists".

Singh criticised its "haste" in praising the election results in Nepal, though the Maoist victory was not a "good sign" for India. The resolution also dubbed the declaration of Nepal as a secular republic "very negative".

"The question is not about ideology but about 'Sanatan Dharma', as the journey of 'Chardhams' is not complete without a trip to Pashupatinath in Nepal," Singh said.

Noting that the Maoists in Nepal have ties with the Naxalites in India, he added: "This is a danger signal to the country whose vast stretches from north to the south are known as the red corridor."

On China, the BJP demanded that the Government "desist from heaping further humiliations on the country" and that it "immediately speed up the construction of infrastructure that our forces need for repulsing foreign troops in the Northeast, particularly in Arunachal and Sikkim". It went on to add that the Government "must come out clearly on the side of the people of Tibet in this hour of their oppression and trial".

Asked if the BJP-led NDA will continue talks with Pakistan if it comes to power, Singh said, "Of course, there is no alternative to peace with Pakistan."

LS preparations on way

•The national executive discussed the ongoing exercise to shortlist candidates for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections. The Indian Express broke the story in the issue dated May 9. The party has asked all state units to send the list of probable candidates to the Central Election Management Committee by this month end. The party had earlier sent observers to 159 constituencies across the country to gain first hand knowledge about the seats and sense the pulse of the electorate. These seats are part of the 297 constituencies shortlisted by the BJP as the ones they should concentrate on as these have been won by the party at least once in the past.

Sushil Modi on agenda today

•The BJP parliamentary board will meet here on Tuesday to discuss the fate of Bihar Deputy CM Sushil Kumar Modi, who's facing a rebellion from his own party MLAs. The BJP brass had asked the 30-odd dissidents to lie low till the national executive, which got over here on Monday. While the party brass believes that Modi allowed the disquiet over the Cabinet reshuffle to worsen, they also contend that a replacement is not going to be easy.

Heading: Secular remarks show BJP’s real face: Cong - Indian Express
Content:
In Delhi for the BJP national executive, newly elected Karnataka CM B S Yeddyurappa on Monday said that the party would replicate the Gujarat growth story in the state. "I will send a team of officials to Gujarat to see the developmental activities there for implementation in Karnataka," he said.

He also vowed to adopt the "Atal Bihari Vajpayee model" in running his government. Asked whether his government would follow the "Hindutva agenda", Yeddyurappa quipped, "development, development and development will be my agenda".

He said he was impressed with former President A P J Abdul Kalam's "Vision 2020" document too and would like to make it a part of his developmental strategy.

The CM also called on Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. The PM assured him of all possible support for the state's development, adding that this was a national priority.

Heading: Law Ministry puts ball back in Raje Govt’s court - Indian Express
Content:
Reacting strongly over the critical references by the BJP on the inclusion of the word 'secular' in the preamble of the Constitution, the Congress on Monday said the Opposition party was trying to undermine the secular fabric of the country.

"Behind the mukhauta (mask), this is the real BJP. They have no right to exist as a political party if they don't subscribe to the basic tenets of the Constitution of India," AICC spokesperson Abhishek Manu Singhvi told reporters here.

In his speech at the BJP national executive on Sunday, party president Rajnath Singh had said there was no need to add 'secular' to the Preamble of the Constitution, done through 42nd amendment in 1976, as it reflected the country's basic character. The BJP president also asked the Government to use panthnirpeksh instead of dharmanirpeksh as the Hindi translation of the word 'secular'.

"Do you believe in sarva dharma sambhaava? Do you believe all religions have the right to preach? The nation wants an answer from the BJP. The BJP represents fundamentalist forces, forces of division," said Singhvi.

The Congress also lauded the results of Assembly and Lok Sabha bypolls in Telangana in which the party won one out of four Lok Sabha seats and six out of 17 Assembly seats. For over two decades, the Congress had been doing poorly in Telangana region.

'RSP's withdrawal due to LF feud'

Taking a dig at the RSP for its decision to withdraw from the UPA-Left Coordination Committee, the Congress on Monday attributed it to the internecine battle in the Left Front, rather than the acts and policies of the UPA Government.

"If there is a local political reason or opportunism or problems in the coalition in West Bengal, they should look into that instead of blaming us," Abhishek Manu Singhvi said.

Heading: Firings: Jaswant takes potshots at CM - Indian Express
Content:
Maintaining its stance that the decision of providing reservation benefits to a particular caste should be taken by the concerned state rather than the Union Government, the Law Ministry on Monday put the ball back into Rajasthan Government's court in the Gurjjar issue.

According to sources, in its reply sent to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Law Ministry maintained that there is a provision in the Constitution for giving quota to a particular community, but the decision has to be taken by the respective state Government. It even referred to the example followed by Maharashtra in a similar situation of extending reservation benefits to the tribals in the state.

The ministry is believed to have said that any state Government which wants to give quota benefits to a community has to justify the decision to the Centre by approaching it with relevant data.

Citing the example of the tribals in Maharashtra, the ministry also pointed towards Article 16 (1) of the Constitution, sources said.

The opinion came following a request by the Prime Minister's Office after Rajasthan Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje wrote a letter to the Prime Minister in the light of violent protests over the quota issue. In her letter, Raje had recommended four to six per cent quota for Gurjjars in the category of de-notified class of tribals/nomadic tribe.

The agitation, spearheaded by Col Kirori Singh Bainsla, has so far left over 43 dead in Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi.

Heading: Mulayam backs ST status - Indian Express
Content: Senior BJP leader Jaswant Singh, a known detractor of Rajasthan Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje, on Monday voiced his unhappiness over the deaths of Gurjjars in police firing in Rajasthan. Suggesting that "we have all become very insensitive", the Leader of the Opposition in Rajya Sabha said this was because the death toll at the end become a mere statistic. "It is a matter of great pain and sorrow," he said about the deaths during the Gurjjar agitation, mostly in police firing. Singh is not in the best of terms with Raje and has earlier openly expressed his displeasure with the state of affairs in the Rajasthan unit of the BJP.

Heading: Post-mortem of agitation victims begins - Indian Express
Content:
Extending full support to the Gurjjar agitation in Rajasthan, Samajwadi Party president Mulayam Singh Yadav on Monday said the community should get Scheduled Tribes status. "The Gurjjar agitation is fully justified... they should get the reservation facility," he said.

Yadav, who was here to unveil a statue of late Prime Minister Chandra Shekhar, said that repression of agitating Gurjjars and firing on them should end immediately. He regretted that "politics has been reduced to personal rivalry today".

Criticising the state Government, he said Dalits are being harassed and the poor are being subjected to immense hardship and are deprived of foodgrains and potable water.

SP general secretary Amar Singh presided over the function.

Heading: Pak bomber targets Danish embassy, kills at least eight - Indian Express
Content:
Eleven days after 16 Gurjjars were killed in police firing in Bayana, three teams of doctors were allowed to conduct the post-mortem on their bodies on Monday.

Gurjjar leader Col Kirori Lal Bainsla agreed to the post-mortem only after laying down conditions in a two-page letter sent to the state administration on Sunday.

Of the 16 bodies, 12 were held by Gurjjar protestors and were kept in a metal trunk with ice flaps. The other four, who died in a local hospital after getting injured in the firing, were released by the local police in the morning.

The post-mortem report was handed over to Col Bainsla, reportedly declaring that all 16 men had died of bullet shots. The post-mortem began in Tilpura where Col Bainsla and agitators have been camping since May 23. The X-ray equipment, used in the post-mortem, was brought from Jaipur in the morning

Meanwhile in Sikandara, out of 20 bodies, post-mortem could be conducted on only three bodies, as the Gurjjar agitators demanded that the examination be done in daylight only. The post-mortem of two bodies lying in Khushali Pura village in Sawai Madhopur district is also likely to be conducted on Tuesday.

The Gurjjar leadership is yet to take a decision on whether to cremate all bodies together or send them to their respective villages. The decision is likely to be taken on Tuesday.

Heading: After Rajnath’s Hindutva, Advani calls for inclusive NDA growth - Indian Express
Content:
At least eight persons were killed and 24 injured when a suicide bomber today blew up his explosive-laden car outside the embassy of Denmark, near the Indian High Commissioner's residence in the Pakistani capital. No group claimed responsibility for the blast but security officials said the attack could be linked to the row over caricatures of the Prophet published in Danish newspapers.

Witnesses said the car drove up and stopped outside the embassy in the upmarket Sector F-6/2, where several diplomatic missions are located, shortly before the blast occurred at about 1 pm.

"It was most likely a suicide blast," said Islamabad SSP Ahmed Latif. Other officials said evidence collected from the site included body parts and ball bearings. Over 30 kg of explosives were packed in the car, they said.

A foreigner, a security guard of the Danish embassy and two policemen were among the dead.

Indian High Commissioner Satyabrata Pal's two-storey residence, known as India House, is located a little over 200 feet from the blast site. Almost all windows panes of the house were shattered. No one within India House was injured.

The attack was condemned by President Pervez Musharraf, Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani and PPP co-chairman Asif Ali Zardari.

Heading: Statue of Shivaji will soon rise, off Mumbai coast, four feet taller than Statue of Liberty - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Janata Party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani today made a strong pitch for expanding the National Democratic Alliance by vigorously pursuing what he called the "good governance agenda" that included development and security as its subtext. This came a day after BJP president Rajnath Singh, in his opening speech, sought to reinforce the Hindutva plank, bringing to the fore its well-worn issues like the abrogation of Article 370, Uniform Civil Code and "secularism that meant 'panthnirpekshta' (instead of 'dharmanirpekshta')." Advani reminded the party that "the expansion, stability and cohesion of the NDA depended on our ability to attract and retain allies who may not be ideologically aligned with the BJP on all issues."

In keeping with this spirit of accommodation, Advani said the party should reach out to "every section of society, including those, such as Muslims and Christians, who have so far remained aloof from the BJP."

"We should emphasise that our party seeks the all-round development and participation of minorities in a non-divisive and integrative agenda without recourse to appeasement or religion-based reservations," Advani said in his concluding speech of the two-day national executive in the capital.

The BJP leader asked the party to draw lessons from the NDA's successful coalition management. "What the people are looking for is a government that can deliver honest and good governance, and make India strong both in development and security. The realization of this truth and the willingness to work together as an alliance on the basis of a common agenda were critical to the success of the NDA in 1998 and 1999," said Advani.

In keeping with his theory that the BJP had helped evolve a bipolar polity in the country, Advani said that the BJP must be in a position to constitute a "robust and unshakable core of the new coalition government". "The BJP's resurgence has become an objective necessity of India's democracy and progress," he said.

Drawing heavily from the successful election management in Gujarat, where the party won a second term under Narendra Modi, Advani told the assembled delegates that "anti-incumbency manifests as a vote against incumbent MLAs and MPs". "Voters' displeasure depends not so much on their representatives' performance in the Assembly or Parliament as on his or her conduct with the people of their constituency. Voters and even karyakartas (workers) punish those who are arrogant, unresponsive, inactive, inaccessible and insincere," he said, adding that the candidate selection in the election-bound states of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh will have to be similar to the one witnessed in Gujarat. A good number of sitting MLAs were dropped in Gujarat to beat the anti-incumbency factor.

He also asked the party to learn from the sound election management and organizational unity, instrumental in party victories in states like Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka.

In the light of a growing personality culture in BJP, Advani called for "firmly curbing the tendency of some functionaries to put their personal interests above the interests of the party."

Terming the party's Karnataka victory as a turning point in Indian politics, "similar to the BJP's quantum leap in 1989 when it increased its tally from two to 84 MPs", he said the challenge before the party is to transform the reality from a frontrunner (as Rajnath called it on Sunday in the context of the next parliamentary elections) to being seen as a "clear winner".

Attacking the Congress on the track-record of the Prime Minister ("doesn't inspire any confidence among the people"), the agrarian crisis ("the government has failed to evolve a long-term strategy to address the crisis") and internal security ("not a single case of terrorist attack in the past four years has been fully investigated and the guilty brought to book"), he said that the UPA-Left arrangement was never cohesive ("they don't see eye to eye on any issue").

He also complimented general secretary (organisation) Ramlal for undertaking the project of booth management committees all across the country. Rajnath has always held that the project is very dear to his heart.

Advani sought to wed the idea of BJP with that of India when he concluded his speech with "Jeetega Bhajapa, Jeetega Bharat" (When the BJP wins, India will win). The slogan was originally used during the Gujarat elections.

Heading: Padma for Hindi writer stolen from train in UP - Indian Express
Content:
The Statue of Liberty is set to be overshadowed, albeit on the other side of the Atlantic. The Congress-NCP alliance government in Maharashtra has decided to install a 309-foot-tall Shivaji statue, four feet taller than the New York monument and the tallest in India — in the Arabian Sea off Mumbai's Marine Drive.

The decision comes days before the manifesto committees of the Congress and NCP are due to meet to review progress on the promises made. It also coincides with the growing clamour to protect the interests of Maharashtrians by Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navnirman Sena and the Shiv Sena.

Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and his deputy R R Patil visited the site with senior officials today and Deshmukh directed his officers to ensure quick clearances for the Rs 200-crore project, officials told The Indian Express.

They said the statue will have a 150-foot-high pedestal on which will be installed a 159-foot-tall bronze of Shivaji riding a horse. That would make it taller than a 30-storey building and the tallest statue in the country, dwarfing the Hanuman statue in New Delhi which is 174 feet tall. It would be among the top 10 tallest statues in the world, a list which is mostly dominated by Buddha statues in east Asia.

The project is estimated to take two years and is subject to environment clearances. Besides, BSNL cables on the seabed will have to be shifted.

The statue was first promised in the Cong-NCP poll manifesto in 2004 but the government's plans to hunt for a location had run into problems. While the Navy refused permission to install it at Oyster Rocks off the eastern coast, the Mumbai Port Trust rejected a second location at Cross Island. The new location finalised today will be at the centre of the curvature of the Queen's Necklace where the state plans to make an artificial island by reclaiming 7.5 acres about 1 km from the shore.

Besides housing the statue, the island will serve as a tourist spot with a sound and light show based on the life of Shivaji, a museum, a library, an eatery and an ornamental garden. A jetty at the National Centre for Performing Arts at the end of Marine Drive will ferry tourists to the island.

Heading: Why Amra Ram Gujar is his community’s new poster-boy - Indian Express
Content:
It's been nearly a week since the Padma Bhushan award conferred on noted Hindi writer Shri Lal Shukla was stolen from the baggage of a Rashtrapati Bhawan official from a moving train, between Etawah and Kanpur. If that's shocking enough, Government Railway Police officials have spent the time trying to figure out who should probe the case.

Shukla could not attend the Padma awards distribution ceremony held on May 5 at Rashtrapati Bhawan due to ill health. Review Officer, Local Commissioner, New Delhi, Uma Pathak was deputed by the President's office to hand over the award to Shukla at his residence in Lucknow.

Pathak took the Farakka Express from New Delhi on May 27, with the award in a bag. According to her complaint, the bag was stolen between 4.30 am and 6 am, while she was sleeping. At Charbagh Railway Station, Lucknow, she informed GRP personnel that the bag was stolen at Panki Railway Station of Kanpur.

GRP authorities at Lucknow transferred the case to their counterparts in Kanpur. After a quick investigation, the Kanpur authorities passed it on the Etawah GRP. And now the GRP at Etawah says they have received no official intimation.

Earlier, following instructions of senior officials at Lucknow, a case under Section 379 of the IPC was registered at the GRP Station at Kanpur Central. Says Inspector Lajja Ram Yadav: "Pathak was mistaken that the theft took place near Panki. Actually the bag was stolen near Phaphund Railway Station, which comes under the Etawah section."

He said the Farakka Express arrives at Kanpur Central at 5.15 am, but on the day the theft took place, the train was two hours late. "When Pathak woke up, she was shocked, and without confirming the fact, she claimed that the theft had taken place near Panki," Yadav said.

Station Officer, GRP, Etawah, Arvind Kumar says he is awaiting official instructions to start the probe. "Whatever I have heard is verbal. Till date I have not received any instructions from my seniors to start the inquiry," he said.

Amidst this blame game, the noted litterateur himself has maintained his calm. "What do I have to do with the theft?" he says. "I have not been deprived of the award, but it has been just delayed due to the theft."

Shukla has earned national and international recognition for his literary works, which include Raag Darbari, Umraonagar Mein Kuchch Din and Suni Ghati ka Suraj. He was conferred the Sahitya Academy Award in 1969 and the Vyas Samman in 1999.

Heading: Deep cleansing - Indian Express
Content:
In the heat of the Gurjjar agitation in Rajasthan, Amra Ram Gujar (31) is a reason to smile for his community, agitating for days for inclusion in the Scheduled Tribe category in Rajasthan.

In Pilupura, Bayana, where hundreds of the community are protesting on the railway tracks, young Gurjjars often quote his name with pride even if the rhetoric is mostly about the "backwardness" of the community.

Gujar, who until recently was just one of the community members lost in daily struggles, rose as a symbol of empowerment in the Gurjjar conscience last month when he cleared the examinations conducted by the Union Public Service Commission for appointment to the Civil Services. And, as it turns out, Gujar, who appeared for the exams as an OBC candidate, is on his way to becoming the first-ever Gurjjar from Rajasthan to join the Indian Administrative Services with an All India Rank of 140. "People at the UPSC have told me that I am going to get IAS rank," he said as he came out of the UPSC building in New Delhi where he went to submit his school certificates on Monday.

The success, Gujar admitted, is a big leap, both for his family and the community, while carefully avoiding questions on the ongoing Gurjjar agitation. "I did not expect to make it to the IAS. At best, I had hoped to make it to the allied services," he added.

Gujar did exceed his own expectations, though. From a government school in Dhunda Lambori village to a college in Rajasthan's Pali district, Gujar didn't let his determination to study further waver even as men from his community carried on with their animal husbandry business. "My father was into tending animals and moving from village to village in search of livelihood," he said.

His eldest brother is still carrying on the family business while one brother works as a helper in a shop in Mumbai and another as constable in Rajasthan Police. Gujar first came to Delhi as a teacher in a municipal school in Sangam Vihar. "I was married when I was 18 and it was important for me to earn as I had a family to look after. I worked as a teacher in an MCD school for two years until 2005 when I moved to Jaipur to join the Rajasthan Police as a sub-inspector," he says.

In the next three years, Gujar appeared for the UPSC exams thrice, while continuing with freak work hours. "I would carry books to office and cut down on my sleeping hours to be able to study," he recalls. Today, his wife back home in Jaipur is busy telling the neighbourhood that her husband is now a 'Collector'. "She is not literate but she does understand that I am going to be an officer now. She is on top of the world," he says.

As for his children, Gujar says he sends all three of them—a daughter (9) and two sons (7 and 5)—to a private school in Jaipur. "I will educate them as well as I can afford. They should do better than me," he says.

Heading: The way of the tiger - Indian Express
Content:
Abir Sabri, celebrated for her alabaster skin, ebony hair, pouting lips and full figure, used to star in racy Egyptian TV shows and movies. Then, at the peak of her career a few years ago, she disappeared — at least her face did. She began performing on Saudi-owned religious TV channels, with her face covered, chanting verses from the Quran. Conservative Saudi Arabian financiers promised her plenty of work, she says, as long as she cleaned up her act. "It's the Wahhabi investors," she says, referring to the strict form of Sunni Islam prevalent in Saudi Arabia. "Before, they invested in terrorism — and now they put their money in culture and the arts."

Egyptians deplore what they call the Saudisation of their culture. Egypt has long dominated the performing arts from Morocco to Iraq, but now petrodollar-flush Saudi investors are buying up the contracts of singers and actors, reshaping the TV and film industries and setting a media agenda rooted more in strict Saudi values than in those of freewheeling Egypt. "As far as I'm concerned, this is the biggest problem in the Middle East right now," says mobile-phone billionaire Naquib Sawiris. "Egypt was always very liberal, very secular and very modern. Now..." He gestures from the window of his 26th-floor Cairo office: "I'm looking at my country, and it's not my country any longer. I feel like an alien here."

At the Grand Hyatt Cairo, a mile upstream along the Nile, the five-star hotel's Saudi owner banned alcohol as of May 1 and ostentatiously ordered its $1.4 million inventory of booze flushed down the drains. "A hotel in Egypt without alcohol is like a beach without a sea," says Aly Mourad, chairman of Studio Masr, the country's oldest film outfit. He says Saudis — who don't even have movie theaters in their own country — now finance 95 per cent of the films made in Egypt. "They say, here, you can have our money, but there are just a few little conditions." More than a few, actually; the 35 Rules, as moviemakers call them, go far beyond predictable bans against on-screen hugging, kissing or drinking. Even to show an empty bed is forbidden, lest it hint that someone might do something on it. Saudi-owned satellite channels are buying up Egyptian film libraries, heavily censoring some old movies while keeping others off the air entirely.

Excerpted from Rod Nordland's 'The last Egyptian belly dancer' in the latest Newsweek

Heading: Pinch of saffron - Indian Express
Content:
One of the most heartrending moments in the Ramayana is the tragic death of Jataayu, the vulture-king, in his vain attempt to defend Sita as she is being abducted by Ravana. "Jataayu-Vadha", the ceremonial enactment of this event, is part of the repertoire of many genres of classical and folk theatre and dance in different parts of the country. Jataayu was a friend of Rama and a decent person pledged to performing his duty, upholding his sacred dharma.

While Jataayu's sorrow-laden tale is part of the mythological, literary, pictorial, sculptural and performing heritage of our land, we are assured by biologists that for millions of years the grand bird has been part of our ecological heritage. And true to Jataayu's promise the Indian vulture has performed its dharma, scavenging and cleaning up our environment. All of a sudden in the last decade of the previous century, our vultures started dying by the hundreds of thousands. When concerned citizens started worrying about the fate of Jataayu's descendants, our government predictably retreated into its usual pattern of denial. India refused to even participate in the international research seeking the causes for the declining vulture population. Nepal and Pakistan took up a more constructive attitude and finally the Peregrine Foundation (certainly not an Indian entity and almost certainly a sinister imperialist neo-colonialist organisation) established that vultures were dying because the carcasses of cattle and sheep (the natural food of the vultures) were full of a chemical called diclonefac. This chemical is a drug prescribed for animals by veterinarians.

Civic organisations like the Bombay Natural History Society started pleading with the government to ban diclonefac, especially because a substitute drug is available. But our noble government in Delhi (which is so quick to make decisions about how many bodyguards to assign to its inflated pompous leadership) kept dithering. Apparently the ministry of environment was in favour of the ban, but other ministries were not. Given that there are hundreds of ministers and three hundred officers of secretary rank in imperial, imperious Delhi, who knows who objected? Suffice it to say that it took almost a decade for our government to impose a weak ban. Dealers who had inventories on their shelves were allowed to continue to sell diclonefac till they exhausted their stocks. We are speedy in banning books or closing down dance-bars; I wonder why this great concern for the dealers of the killer chemical? The tragedy is that there is another drug appropriate for human prescription which contains diclonefac. Veterinarians and farmers have simply switched to this one and the ban on diclonefac is not working.

At first I thought that the powerful lobby of diclonefac manufacturers must have lobbied and fixed the system against the vultures who have neither votes nor lobbying power. But it turns out that this is not the case as the revenue from this drug is not of material consequence to the industry. The real problem, we are told, is that the substitute drug is more expensive and therefore inimical to the interests of our noble kisaans. When I was informed about this, I could not stop laughing for several minutes. Here is a government that spends Rs 200,000 crore (or is it Rs 300,000 crore?) on subsidies and which writes off Rs 60,000 crore of loans and it does not have a measly few tens of crores to subsidise the environmentally safe substitute for diclonefac.

To love a country means that one loves not just the pursuit of power in its capital city. To love India is to love her hills, valleys, plains, plateaux, estuaries, deltas, marshlands, deserts, rivers, lakes, water-bodies, habitations and wildernesses and of course to love the plants, trees, animals and birds that have been with us mythologically and biologically for ever. It is this love that our clever leaders seem to lack. The finance minister announced funding for a tiger protection force in his recent budget speech. There has been no movement since then. The proposed funding will doubtless be returned at the end of the fiscal year with appropriate deductions for tea, biscuits and airfares for committees (or should we call them commissions or better still "task forces" to suit the linguistic sensibilities of the consultants who are popular with our ministers and secretaries).

And yet there is no excuse at all. We can so easily subsidise diclonefac's substitute, we can so easily pay decent salaries and provide needed equipment to our forest guards. Leftists will not object; the NDA will not obstruct; WTO will not penalise and it will cost less than the annual ministerial/secretarial travel bills of just one department in Delhi. Are our leaders determined to go down in history as they who presided over the extinction of the tiger and the vulture? Are they not scared of Jataayu's curse as we poison his descendants?

Our son Raghav is currently engaged in "doing" a project on vultures as part of the compulsory "environmental studies" subject in his syllabus. If only the HRD ministry could set the syllabus and save our wild-life, how wonderful would our country be? I was explaining to him that some thirty odd years ago I was living in the Cumballa Hill area of Bombay (sorry Mumbai) and from our balcony we could see magnificent specimens of these mighty birds hovering around the Parsee Tower of Silence. They are all gone today and that ancient people have to violate their religious precepts and cremate their dead. Being young he is yet to turn cynical. He draws comfort from the fact that voluntary citizens organisations in our country like the Bombay Natural History Society and overseas like the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds are working on "captive breeding" of vultures although they are yet to see much success. He argues that civic action can substitute government apathy.

I just worry that his children will have to rest content with paintings of Jataayu and photographs of the great Indian vulture. The live models will have disappeared for good.

The writer divides his time between Mumbai and Bangalore jerry.rao@expressindia.com

Heading: TRS trips and falls - Indian Express
Content:
India's national parties are nonpareil when it comes to crushingly disappointing those who have a stake in intelligent politics. These columns have despaired over the Congress's strange misreading of political trends. The BJP, we had noted, had at least got the bit about projecting regional party leaders right. Now the BJP hastens to prove that any thought about its political cleverness following the dramatic Karnataka win is premature. Its national executive saw the party dusting off the old chestnuts like Article 370 and the uniform civil code. If state poll victories are going to induce in the party such juvenile muscle flexing, the BJP can write an early obituary about its plans of forming a national grand alliance. Surely even the most ideologically "pure" of BJP strategists don't think that vox populi is warming to the idea of handing the BJP a single-party mandate.

What is especially puzzling is that the BJP's successful campaign in Karnataka was in part built by keeping out pet party issues. It clearly worked, even when the BJP was fighting alone. So why on earth would the party want to start its national campaign — that is what the national executive was all about — differently, more so when the Congress seems incapable right now of even explaining why it lost Karnataka or several other states. This is, in fact, not as puzzling as it may appear. Within the BJP, factional battles often come disguised as debates on core ideology. And it is an open secret that the party has through its string of victories in state elections been a divided house, between the BJP president, Rajnath Singh, and its prime ministerial candidate, L.K. Advani.

Left unresolved for long this factional struggle would deny the BJP a chance, perhaps the best chance in its short history, of becoming a non-sectarian party of the centre-right, of rediscovering its earlier instinctive support for economic liberalism. The Congress has shown that tacking to the left on economic policy doesn't bring electoral dividends. That should make the BJP think hard about how to politically dress up an economic message that emphasises non-state actors and actions. The party can be centre-of-rightish on national security and indeed on Kashmir policy without add-ons like Article 370. It retains its character and it doesn't put off potential allies who are otherwise warming to the BJP's poll successes — this is a no-brainer, surely? But organisations focused on a daily reading of which of its competing leaders is ahead cannot be counted upon to see that.

Heading: This second energy crisis - Indian Express
Content:
The Telagana Rashtriya Samiti (TRS) is left dazed and confused by its staggeringly subpar performance in the Andhra bypolls, and understandably so. These elections were supposed to be a referendum on the Telangana statehood issue, announced after the TRS pulled out its MPs and MLAs, claiming that the UPA and YRS government in Andhra Pradesh were insufficiently committed to the Telangana cause they had promised to support in 2004. When he promised to settle the matter in "the people's court", TRS leader Chandrasekhar Rao certainly didn't expect this tremendous whack — only last year he had resigned and been re-elected by a large margin of over 200,000 votes. This time, he managed a meagre 15,000, and the TRS lost five of its Assembly seats to the Congress and four to the TDP.

So as it turns out, maybe the elections were a referendum on political drama and instability. The TRS has proved to be a volatile partner, sparring with the UPA and withdrawing support at key moments. Perhaps this result signals the voters' impatience with a party with a perpetual attention problem, one that periodically plunges the state into uncertainty just to display its own muscle. The Telangana region has been historically held back by social and economic underdevelopment, and the Telangana protest is not just a simple insistence on its own address but also a demand for developmental redress. So the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which promised to tackle specific deliverables like unemployment, drinking water and power supply issues, struck the right chords while the TRS's grand blueprint for a separate Telangana was left in tatters, at least for the time being.

So what's the moral of the story? If anything, it is the fact that the Indian voter cannot be gulled by identity politics much longer, unless backed by a positive development agenda. Manifestoes and vague promises of a coming utopia just don't cut it, without a measurable governance record. Many states have seen a winnowing out of the weaker players, as voters overwhelmingly cast their lot with parties and coalitions that promised stability and a concrete plan. The TRS would do well to realise that temperamental and confrontational politics can only get it so far — from now on, it needs a more grown-up vision for change.

Heading: Neighbourly charity - Indian Express
Content:
We are facing two problems. One is imported energy, the other is macro imbalance.
